Tickets are available online through the **BudapestGO App**.\n\n💡 **Local Tip**: If you visit the Hungarian capital for **2-3 days** and you stay in a [city center hotel](https://www.budapestbylocals.com/budapest-city-centre-hotels/), we recommend that you use:\n\nTime-based tickets (30-minute and 90-minute) work well too with unlimted transfers within the timeframe.\n\nSingle tickets or the\n\nDiscounted block of 10 tickets to make travelling on public transport lines hassle-free.\n\n### Free Travel For Seniors 65 + – EU Citizens Only\n**TIP:** Citizens of the **European Union** countries and Switzerland **aged 65** and up can use all public transport lines for **free** in Budapest.\n\nThey have to show a **valid ID** to verify age and nationality if asked by a ticket inspector).\n\nThe current tickets and passes are of **pale purple** colour.\n\n### Tickets, Transfer Tickets\n![photo of a public transport single ticket](https://budapestbylocals.b-cdn.net/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/single_ticket_budapest_public_transport.webp)_Single Ticket – 500 HUF_\n\n## ✈ Public Transport Services From Airport To The City Centre\n### 100E Airport Express Shuttle Bus To The City Center/Deák Ferenc Square\n#### You Need To Purchase A Separate Single Ticket (2 500 HUF)\n- Ferenc Liszt Airport and\n- Deák Ferenc tér metro hub (where 3 metro lines – M1, M2, M3 – meet) in district V, downtown Budapest\n\n## Buying Public Transport Tickets/Passes at Budapest Airport\nYou can buy\n\n### Relay Newsstands (sell only single tickets/pack of 10 single tickets):\n**Opening hours** of the ticket office at the Kőbánya Kispest Metro Termini: every day: 6.00-21.30.\n\n## 🚃 Suburban Railway (HÉV)\nYou can travel by **HÉV** (green trains) to the outskirts of Budapest.\n\n![budapest public transport suburban railway](https://budapestbylocals.b-cdn.net/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/budapest_public_transport_suburban_railway.webp)\n\nThe Szentendre line might be interesting for tourists. It runs between Batthyány tér (it’s also on the red metro line) and Szentendre.\n\n**Szentendre** is a small, charming town right on the Danube bank. Don’t miss visiting it if you come to Budapest for a couple of days!\n\nTickets within the boundary of the city cost the same as discussed above. Outside Budapest you pay according to the distance you’ll cover during your trip.\n\nWithin Budapest (Batthyány tér – Békásmegyer), your normal single ticket or travel pass is valid. Beyond the city boundary, from Békásmegyer to Szentendre, you need a supplementary HÉV ticket, which costs 560 HUF. HÉV trains run every 10 to 30 minutes.",

        "markdown": "Last Updated on 5 August 2026 by [ZoliBP](https://www.budapestbylocals.com/budapest-public-transport/#bbl-author-bio)\n\nLast Updated on 5 August 2026 by [ZoliBP](https://www.budapestbylocals.com/budapest-public-transport/#bbl-author-bio)\n\n![A tram and bus on the streets of Budapest, showing the city's public transport network](<Base64-Image-Removed>)\n\n## How to Travel in the City?\n\nUse **public transport services** to travel in Budapest, especially if you stay in one of the outer districts.\n\nAlthough attractions in the central districts (V., VI., parts of I., II., VII. and VIII.) are easy to explore **on foot** you might want to rest your legs after a while and hop on a metro/tram/bus.\n\nTable of Contents – Budapest Public Transport+\n\n## Best Public Transport Lines For Tourists\n\nYou will easily get to any sight and attraction by travelling on one of the **four metro lines** or the major tram lines (No. 4, 6 and 2).\n\n💡 **Local Tip**: In case it’s cold or a summer shower catches you, take one of the **four metro lines** (M1 **,** M2, M3 and M4), or any of the major tram lines (tram 2, 2B, , 4, 6, 47, 49 or 19)\n\n- **Trams No. 2 and 2B** run along the Pest Danube embankment (between Jászai Mari tér – Közvágóhíd stops), covering the picturesque promenade called Duna Corso and stopping in front of the Parliament in Kossuth Square.\n- **Trams 47** and **49** are also useful especially if you want to get from Pest to Buda or vice versa.\n- **Tram 19** is great for **sightseeing in Buda**, it connects Kelenföld Train Station with Óbuda (the Northern part of Buda). Similarly to Tram 2 and 2B in Pest it travels along the Danube between Liberty Bridge and Margaret Bridge offering a scenic view of the river and some famous attractions in Pest, in the .\n\n[See more on travelling buy tram in Budapest!](https://www.budapestbylocals.com/budapest-public-transport/2/#trams)\n\nThese transport services will take you to most of the places of interest.\n\nThe bus and trolley bus service are quite extensive too.\n\nThere’s also a scheduled **boat service** on the Danube from spring till autumn.\n\nBelow you find information on Budapest public transport: types of **tickets** and passes, buying, and validating them.\n\n![trams 4 and 6 in Budapest on a rainy day](https://budapestbylocals.b-cdn.net/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/trams_budapest23.webp)_Tram 4 Along Grand Boulevard_\n\n## A Few Things Worth Booking While You’re Here\n\nSince you’re already planning how to get around, here are a few popular extras that pair well with a Budapest trip — all bookable online in advance.\n\n#### Budapest Discovery Cruise\n\nThe cheapest way to see the city’s landmarks from the Danube – a 50-minute sightseeing loop under all six bridges.\n\nFrom €7\n\n[Check Availability](https://budapestxplore.com/en/16-00-cruise-xpYzBhZDNmND?affi=7639)\n\n#### Széchenyi Thermal Bath\n\nEurope’s largest spa complex – soak in the famous outdoor pools right in the City Park.\n\nFrom €28\n\n[Check Tickets](https://budapestxplore.com/en/entrance-to-szechenyi-spa-xpYmYYEyMzhh?affi=7639)\n\n#### Shared Airport Shuttle\n\nSkip the public bus with your luggage – a shared shuttle takes you door-to-door between the airport and your address.\n\nFrom €17\n\n[Check Availability](https://gyg.me/UYDVGbWS)\n\n## Tickets, Travel Cards, Prices and Fines\n\n**Quick price overview** (see full details below)\n\nSingle Ticket500 HUF700 HUF on board\n\nBlock of 104 500 HUF450 HUF each\n\n30-Minute Ticket600 HUFunlimited transfers\n\n90-Minute Ticket850 HUFunlimited transfers\n\n24-Hour Travel Card2 750 HUFunlimited travel\n\n72-Hour Travel Card5 750 HUFunlimited travel\n\nBudapest has a fairly extensive and efficient public transport system. It is also **cheaper** than in most Western European cities.\n\nA wide variety of **trams, buses, trolleys** and **metro trains** run in the city.\n\nNight service is quite reliable, too.\n\n![two trams (No. 47) and a blue bus in Budapest](https://budapestbylocals.b-cdn.net/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/budapest_public_transport23.webp)\n\n📋 **Note:** Be prepared for typical **rush hours**: vehicles are crowded and traffic can be rather slow. This would be expected in any large city.\n\n## Children’s Fares, Student Passes, Family Discounts\n\nChildren living in Hungary up to the **age of 14** travel free of charge. A valid Hungarian identity card is required for them to verify age if a controller asks for tickets and passes.\n\nPupils, university **students** can buy discount monthly/yearly passes with a valid student ID card.\n\nNo student discount on single tickets though.\n\n💡 **Local Tip**: For **families visiting Budapest** with kids we recommend getting the 24-hour group travel card. 5 people can travel with it for up to 24 hours and it costs 5 000 HUF.\n\n### Free Travel on Public Transport with Budapest Card\n\n💡 **Local Tip**: If you don’t want to bother with buying and validating tickets, [purchase a Budapest City Card](https://gyg.me/a7D4aHNN).\n\nBesides unlimited free travel on public transport, the card offers a range of **discounts** on tours/services, free entry to the permanent exhibitions of many museums, entry to the Lukács Bath etc.\n\n## Buy Budapest Card: Public Transport, 30+ Top Attractions & Tours\n\n![Budapest Cards](https://budapestbylocals.b-cdn.net/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/budapest_card_public_transport.webp)_Budapest Cards_\n\n24-Hour Card17 990 HUFClassic\n\n48-Hour Card23 990 HUFClassic\n\n72-Hour Card29 990 HUFClassic\n\n96-Hour Card38 990 HUFClassic\n\n72-Hour Plus39 990 HUFmore inclusions\n\n72-Hour Flexi27 990 HUFflexible use\n\nThere’s also a dedicated **Sziget Citypass by Budapest Card** for festival-goers: 2-day pass 14 990 HUF, 7-day pass 29 990 HUF.\n\nPowered by [GetYourGuide](https://www.getyourguide.com/budapest-l29/)\n\nRead more [about the Budapest Card and whether it’s worth getting it!](https://www.budapestbylocals.com/budapest-card/)\n\n## Public Transport Tickets and Passes\n\n**_(Current Prices)_**\n\n📋 **Note:** A **single ticket costs 500 HUF** (700 HUF if bought on board), and a pack of 10 single tickets costs 4 500 HUF. Prices are reviewed periodically by BKK, so always check the [official BKK price list](https://bkk.hu/en/tickets-and-passes/prices/) for the latest figures. Tickets are available online through the **BudapestGO App**.\n\n💡 **Local Tip**: If you visit the Hungarian capital for **2-3 days** and you stay in a [city center hotel](https://www.budapestbylocals.com/budapest-city-centre-hotels/), we recommend that you use:\n\nTime-based tickets (30-minute and 90-minute) work well too with unlimted transfers within the timeframe.\n\nSingle tickets or the\n\nDiscounted block of 10 tickets to make travelling on public transport lines hassle-free.\n\n### Free Travel For Seniors 65 + – EU Citizens Only\n\n**TIP:** Citizens of the **European Union** countries and Switzerland **aged 65** and up can use all public transport lines for **free** in Budapest.\n\nThey have to show a **valid ID** to verify age and nationality if asked by a ticket inspector).\n\nThe current tickets and passes are of **pale purple** colour.\n\n### Tickets, Transfer Tickets\n\n- **Single ticket** (vonaljegy or just jegy) 500 HUF, (700 HUF if purchased from the driver on board the vehicle): valid on all public transport vehicles for one uninterrupted trip. If you\n- **Block of 10 single tickets** (tíz darabos gyűjtőjegy: 4 500 HUF). Costs less than 10 single tickets purchased individually.\n\n![photo of a public transport single ticket](https://budapestbylocals.b-cdn.net/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/single_ticket_budapest_public_transport.webp)_Single Ticket – 500 HUF_\n\n### Time-Based Tickets: Save Money\n\nUse time-based tickets if you need to **transfer** between metro lines and also other lines (trams, buses, trolley).\n\nYou save money with it since you don’t need to use a 500-HUF single ticket every time you need to change public transport lines.\n\nMoreover, you can **finish** your trip beyond the 30th or 90th minute until you reach your destination within Budapest.\n\nPlease remember to **validate** your time-based ticket before the start of your travel and each time you switch to another travel line.\n\n![a hand holding a mobile phone and preparing to scan a public transport ticket on the door of a tram](https://budapestbylocals.b-cdn.net/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/time_based_budapest_public_travel_ticket.webp)_Validating A Ticket with a Mobile_\n\nYou can use time-based tickets for an unlimited number of transfers and trip interruptions, by validating it each time you board making sure that your last transfer falls within the 30-minute or 90-minute time limit.\n\n#### There Are Two Time-Based Tickets:\n\n- 30-minute ticket: 600 HUF\n- 90-minute ticket: 850 HUF\n\n📋 **Important!** Please **scan the code** each time when you board a vehicle to validate your ticket. When transferring between metrolines, you are not required to revalidate your ticket.\n\n📋 **Note:** If you carry a bike with you (permitted only on a few vehicle types) you have to validate a single ticket for it.\n\n## Travel Cards\n\n### 24-Hour Travel Card\n\n- Price: 2 750 HUF – Please note that is **not the same as the 24-hour Budapest Card**\n- Valid on all public transport vehicles except for the boat service on the Danube.\n- For an unlimited number of trips from 0:00 to 24:00 of the day indicated on the ticket (you decide on the starting time).\n\n![photo of a 24-hour Budapest Public Transport travel card (pale purple)](https://budapestbylocals.b-cdn.net/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/24hour_budapest_public_transport_card.webp)_24-Hour Travel Card_\n\n### 72-Hour Travel Card\n\n- Price: 5 750 HUF – **not the same as the 72-hour Budapest Card**\n- Valid on all public transport vehicles – except for the boat service- for an unlimited number of trips for 72 hours starting from the time and date you purchased it.\n\n## Public Boat Service Tickets\n\nUnfortunately Public Boat services ceased to run as of 2023 due to high maintenance expenses.\n\n## Where To Buy Tickets And Passes?\n\nYou have two options, choose the one that you’re more comfortable with:\n\n### BudapestGO App or Paper Tickets/Travel Cards\n\n- Go the traditional way and buy and use **paper tickets** and **travel cards** (24-hour or 72-hour, or if you are comfortable with using apps\n- [Download the BudapestGO public transport application](https://bkk.hu/en/tickets-and-passes/budapestgo/) to buy single tickets, time based tickets (for 30-minute or 90-minute duration) and 24/72-hour travel cards. The app is also a great help in planning your route providing real-time travel information as well as route and service recommendations including the BuBi public bike rental points.\n\n![photo showing a hand holding a mobile phone on a bus](https://budapestbylocals.b-cdn.net/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/budapestgo_app.webp)BudapestGO App\n\nYou can buy **paper tickets** and travel cards from the [ticket vending machines with bankcard (or cash)](https://www.budapestbylocals.com/budapest-public-transport/#how-to-use-the-ticket-vending-machines-tv-ms). You The purple colored ticket automats are placed at main public transport stations (metro entrance), as well as at the airport.\n\nThe airport also has **BKK Customer Sales Points** where you can get your ticket/travel card from a real person.\n\n![three young people buying tickets from a ticket vending machine](https://budapestbylocals.b-cdn.net/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/publicktransport_ticket_vending_machine_budapest.webp)\n\nIf you don’t have or don’t want to use the **BudapestGO App** you have to buy your tickets/pass in advance.\n\nYou can get them from **ticket vending machines** (TVM) or at many newspaper kiosks.\n\nAround 300 new ticket vending machines have been placed throughout the city where you can get tickets and passes 24/7 by paying with cash or bank card.\n\nI often use them and found them are **quite reliable**.\n\nMost **ticket offices** have closed down though. You will find Ticket Offices (Jegypénztár) in **some metro stations** near the entrance:\n\n![front photo of a public transport ticket vending machine in Budapest](https://budapestbylocals.b-cdn.net/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/ticket_vending_machines.webp)_Ticket Vending Machine_\n\n- Corvin negyed M3/blue line,\n- Népliget M3/blue line,\n- Nyugati tér M3/blue line,\n- Blaha Lujza tér M2/red line,\n- Széll Kálmán tér M2/red line.\n\nMost **cashiers** speak only Hungarian so it’s best to go to the cashier with a piece of paper on which you’ve written down in Hungarian what type of ticket you want to buy.\n\n💡 **Local Tip**: Here is a [map of the Public Transport Company showing all the operating ticket sellers](https://bkk.hu/pontkereso/).\n\n## How To Use The Ticket Vending Machines (TVMs)?\n\nUsing the machines is pretty straightforward, just read the instructions displayed on the monitor.\n\nFirst **choose language** by touching the appropriate flag symbol on the bottom of the screen on the right hand side of the TVM.\n\nA list of the **most popular ticket types** and passes will appear\n\n- Single ticket-500 HUF,\n- Block of 10 tickets – 4500 HUF,\n- 24-hour travel card,\n- 24-hour group travel card,\n- Various monthly passes.\n\nI only give you the steps on buying tickets/travel card because these are the ones most suited to tourists visiting Budapest for a couple of days.\n\n![Photo showing the touch screen of the public transport ticket vending machine](https://budapestbylocals.b-cdn.net/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/ticket_vending_machine_budapest02.webp)_Touch Screen Of The Ticket Vending Machine_\n\n### Buying Ticket/Travel Card From The TVM:\n\n- **Select** the ticket/travel card you want to buy.\n- Decide whether you want the machine to print an **invoice**, if not then press payment without VAT invoice.\n- Choose **payment** method: you can pay by cash, bank card (PayPass/contactless cards). I prefer using bank card, and **recommend** this payment method for tourists as well.\n\n#### Paying By Bank Card/Contactless Card – Recommended For Tourists\n\nThe simplest and fastest way is to pay with a **bankcard/contactless card**.\n\nJust follow the steps shown on the card terminal screen. After payment collect the purchased ticket or travel card.\n\n#### Paying By Cash:\n\nThe machine accepts all current Hungarian **coins** from 5 HUF to 200 HUF.\n\nYou can use **banknotes** too: 500 HUF, 1 000 HUF, 2 000 HUF, 5 000 HUF, 10 000 HUF, 20 000 HUF. Based on the total value of the purchase the TVM defines the banknotes to be accepted.\n\nIf the purchase is of a small amount (e.g. a 500 HUF single ticket) 2000 HUF or smaller notes are accepted. In case of a bigger purchase larger notes can also be used.\n\nThe machine accepts 35 coins and 15 banknotes per transaction. It gives back changes in coins and notes.\n\nMake sure you **don’t leave your bank card** or other **belongings** at the machine.\n\nYou can also view an [instructional video](https://bkk.hu/en/tickets-and-passes/ticket-vending-machines-tvm/) on how to buy monthly passes and use the vending machines on the transport company’s (BKK) website.\n\n## How To Validate Tickets?\n\nYou must validate your ticket at the start of your journey.\n\n### Metro Stations\n\nIn case of **metro tickets** you have to put the ticket in the ticket validation machine (orange coloured box on a metal pole) that’ll stamp a time and date on the ticket.\n\nA short musical tone and the tiny green light confirm that the ticket has been validated.\n\nOnce you validated the metro ticket you head for the **escalator** that’ll take you to the metro platform where you wait for the metro car.\n\nAt the top of the escalator **ticket inspectors** will most likely stop you to check whether you’ve validated your ticket.\n\n![an infograph showing how to validate public transport tickets in Budapest](https://budapestbylocals.b-cdn.net/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/budapest_public_transport_ticket_validation.webp)Remember To Validate Your Ticket\n\n![photo showing a hand inserting a metro ticket in the orange-coloured validating machine](https://budapestbylocals.b-cdn.net/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/metro_ticket_validation_budapest.webp)_Validating A Ticket At the Metro_\n\n### Other Vehicles\n\nOn other vehicles (trams, buses, trolley) there’ s\n\n- Either the **orange or yellow box** similar to the ones in metro stations, or\n- A smaller red box in which you insert the ticket then pull the black part on the top towards you to punch the ticket (a pattern of holes appear on the validated ticket).\n\n📋 **Note:** The slot on some ticket validation machines is clogged with chewing gum or paper (deliberately done by prank makers) so you won’t be able to insert the ticket. Try another machine on the vehicle to validate your ticket.\n\nInspectors check passengers’ tickets throughout the day.\n\nAn inspector usually wears dark blue **uniform** and a blue with a red armband. Nowadays, however they are in plain clothes (but still must put on the armband when checking tickets) in order to disguise themselves.\n\nTo **avoid problems**, buy the type of ticket or pass that are most suitable for your visit and your budget, and remember to validate it. Keep your ticket until the end of your journey.\n\n**Fines** are high (if caught travelling without a valid ticket or pass you’ll be fined to pay 25 000 HUF, reduced to 12 000 HUF if you pay it on the spot or within 2 days of being fined)\n\nIt’s not worth ruining your stay with constant watching out for the inspectors. If you forgot to buy a ticket or **validate** it, and you’re fined the ticket inspector must give you a receipt about the payment.\n\n## Fines For Travelling Without A Valid Ticket/Pass\n\nIf you’re caught without a valid ticket by a **ticket inspector**, you are to [pay a fine](https://www.budapestbylocals.com/budapest-public-transport/#fines) which is currently **12 000 HUF** paid on the spot or in BKK’s Surcharge Office within 2 work days from the date of the fining.\n\n**Note:** The inspector must give you a receipt of the payment when you pay on the spot.\n\nIf you don’ pay the fine on the spot or within 2 work days, but settle the amount within 30 days the penalty fare is **25 000 HUF**.\n\nIf you don’t pay the fine on the spot, the ticket inspector initiates a **fining procedure** (ensuring the opportunity of deferred payment).\n\n![A ticket inspctor (head is not shown in the photo) looking for something in his purse](https://budapestbylocals.b-cdn.net/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/penalty_budapest_public_transport.webp)_A Ticket Inspector On A Tram_\n\nIn this case he/she is entitled to ask the required personal data (name, mother’s name, date and place of birth) and also the address of the passenger. On the basis of these data, the ticket inspector fills in a so-called “Surcharging procedure report”.\n\nIf the passenger refuses to give his/her personal data, the ticket inspector can ask for **police assistance** on the spot.\n\nThe ticket inspector gives a **cheque** about the amount of the fine and a leaflet about the opportunities of payment.\n\nThe passenger shall sign that he/she accepts the surcharging and confirms that he/she has given the required personal data. The denial of signature doesn’t acquit the passenger of the consequences of the fining.\n\nYou’ll find the most up-to-date **information** about tickets, [prices and penalty fines on the Public Transport Company’s website (BKK).](https://bkk.hu/en/tickets-and-passes/information-about-penalty-fares/)\n\n## ✈ Public Transport Services From Airport To The City Centre\n\n### 100E Airport Express Shuttle Bus To The City Center/Deák Ferenc Square\n\n#### You Need To Purchase A Separate Single Ticket (2 500 HUF)\n\nThe 100E Airport Express is a direct bus line that connects the Airport and the City Centre. The journey takes **40 minutes** only.\n\nBuses – low-floor, air-conditioned vehicles run **every 6-8 minutes** during the day and every 10 minutes at night in the tourist season\n\n- Ferenc Liszt Airport and\n- Deák Ferenc tér metro hub (where 3 metro lines – M1, M2, M3 – meet) in district V, downtown Budapest\n\nThe bus also stops at **Kálvin tér** (M3 metro) and Astoria (M2 metro). See the [schedule on BKK’s website](https://bkk.hu/en/travel-information/public-transport/airport-shuttle/).\n\nThe first bus departs at **03:40 AM** the last one at **01.20 AM** (runs every 20 min).\n\n![the blue 100E Airport Express shuttle bus in front of Budapest Airport terminal 2A](https://budapestbylocals.b-cdn.net/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/100E_budapest_airport_express.webp)_100E Airport Express Bus_\n\n### Where To Buy Ticket For The 100E Airport Express Bus?\n\nThe new bus service can be used with a **special ticket** that is valid only for this line. A one-way ride costs **2 500 HUF (cc. 6.2 EUR).** _(The Budapest Card and other passes aren’t valid for this service)_.\n\n**Note:** The Airport Shuttle bus ticket can be bought\n\n- At the BKK Customer Service Points at the Airport or\n- From **Ticket vending machines** located next to the Customer Service (accepts credit card/bank card).\n- You can also buy it **on board the bus** in digital form through the yellow and black Budapest Pay & Go devices, with a bankcard or smart watch or phone.\n\nYour ticket purchase also **validates** your ticket.\n\n![picture showing how to use the Budapest Pay & Go ticket purchase device for the 100E Airport Shuttle Bus](https://budapestbylocals.b-cdn.net/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/budapest_airport_express_ticket_purchase.webp)_Buyig Your 100E Airport Bus Ticket Onboard The Bus_\n\nIn case a ticket inspector comes and asks for your ticket just touch your bankcard/smartwatch/smartphone you used to pay with to the back of the handheld gadget the controller has with her/him.\n\nSee [where to buy tickets at the airport](https://www.budapestbylocals.com/budapest-public-transport/#publictransportticketsattheairport)!\n\n## Other Ways To Get To the City Center/Airport\n\nYou can choose from several ways to travel to the centre from [Budapest Airport](https://www.budapestbylocals.com/budapest-airport/):\n\n- **Train service from Ferihegy Train Station** (accessible by bus 200E during the day, and by bus 900 at night from Liszt Ferenc Airport Terminal 2, the trip is 5 stops, around 10 minutes) to Western Train Station (Nyugati Pályaudvar): this is the simplest way to get to the [city centre](https://www.budapestbylocals.com/budapest-city-centre/).\n- You can get to the city center by the **M3 (blue) metro line** or trams 4 and 6 from the train station. The train journey takes less than half an hour (cc. 22-25 minutes).\n- **Train tickets** (costs cc. 400 HUF) can be purchased at the ticket office at Ferihegy train station (open: 6.00-18.00 every day) or from ticket vending machines.\n- [Travel cards (24-hour, 72-hour)](https://www.budapestbylocals.com/budapest-public-transport/#publictransportticketsattheairport) are also valid for the train trip between Ferihegy and Nyugati Train Stations (and for buses 200 E/900). If you don’t have a travel card or don’t want to buy it then you’ll need a [single ticket](https://www.budapestbylocals.com/budapest-public-transport/#publictransportticketsattheairport)(costs 500 HUF, 700 HUF if bought on board the bus) for the bus trip from Terminal 2 to Ferihegy Train Station.\n- **Bus 200E** takes you from Terminal 2 to the M3 (blue) metro terminal called Kőbánya-Kispest Metro Station. The bus operates from 4.00 till 23.00 daily. The journey is about **30 minutes.** From there you can travel on by metro. See [timetable of Bus200E](https://bkk.hu/en/timetables/).\n\n![front view of the blue Bus 200E at a bus stop](https://budapestbylocals.b-cdn.net/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/budapest_bus200E_airport_city_centre.webp)_Bus 200E – Airport-City Centre Connection_\n\nA one-way public transport ticket (single ticket) costs 500 HUF (700 HUF when you buy it from the driver onboard the bus).\n\n## Buying Public Transport Tickets/Passes at Budapest Airport\n\nYou can buy\n\n- 100E Airport Express shuttle bus ticket (Bus No. 100E) – 2 500 HUF\n- Single tickets (500 HUF),\n- Pack of 10 single tickets (4 500 HUF),\n- Travel cards (24-hour, 72-hour),\n- Monthly, yearly etc. passes\n\nat the **BKK Customer Points**/BKK Ügyfélpont at Terminal 2A and 2B. (BKK is an abbreviation for the Budapest Publc Transport Company in Hungarian).\n\nYou can also use the **Ticket Vending Machines** palced next to the customer service point.\n\n![public transport tickets budapest airport](https://budapestbylocals.b-cdn.net/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/public_transport_tickets_budapest_airport.webp)_BKK Customer Service Point at the Airport_\n\n### BKK Customer Service at the Airport – Opening Hours\n\n- **Terminal 2A, Arrivals**, Opening Hours: every day: 08.00 – 22.00, on December 31: 08.00 – 20.00, on January 01: 08.00 – 22.00\n- **Terminal 2B, Arrivals**, Opening Hours: every day: 09.00 – 21.00, on December 31: 08.00 – 21.00, on January 01: 09.00 – 21.00\n\n### Ticket Vending Machines  – Next to the Customer Service Point\n\nYou can buy\n\n- tickets,\n- travel cards and\n- the airport bus ticket (Bus No. 100E, 2 500 HUF) from **3 ticket vending machines** next to the customer service center (accepts bank card/credit card).\n\n### News Agent, Post Office\n\nYou can also buy single tickets and pack of 10 single tickets at\n\n- the **Relay News Agents**\n- and at the **post office** (closed on weekends and holidays) on the mezzanine level at Terminal 2A. Opening Hours of the Post Office: Monday – Friday: 8.00 – 12.00 and 12.30 – 15.30, **closed** on weekends and public holidays. 24-hour, 72-hour and 7-day **travel cards** are also sold at the post office at Terminal 2A.\n\n### Relay Newsstands (sell only single tickets/pack of 10 single tickets):\n\n- Terminal 2A Arrivals, Relay Newsstand: 08.30 – 00.30 every day\n- Terminal 2A Departures, Relay Newsstand: 04.15 – 21.00 every day\n- Terminal 2B Arrivals, Relay Newsstand: 08.00 – 21.30 every day\n- Terminal 2B Departures, Relay Newsstand: 04.30-21.00 every day\n- [Skycourt](https://www.budapestbylocals.com/skycourt-budapest/), Relay: Mon-Fri: 04.15 – 21.00 every day, Sat: 04.15 – 20.00\n\n**Opening hours** of the ticket office at the Kőbánya Kispest Metro Termini: every day: 6.00-21.30.\n\n### Ticket Vending Machine (Bus 200E Stop)\n\nThere’s also a ticket vending machine at the stop of Bus 200E. You can buy tickets (all types), travel cards and passes here with cash or bank card.\n\n📋 **Note:** Remember to **validate your ticket**, travel cards don’t require validation, you just have to show them to the inspector if asked.\n\nRead about [other ways of getting to the city centre from Liszt Ferenc Airport.](https://www.budapestbylocals.com/budapest-airport/#publictransport)\n\n## Budapest Metro Lines\n\n![budapest by metro](https://budapestbylocals.b-cdn.net/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/budapest_by_metro.webp)_M2, Red Metro Line In Budapest_\n\nThe 4-line metro system is **efficient** and clean. Trains run from 4.30 am to 11.10 pm.\n\nThe **newest, 4th line** started operation at end of March in 2014 with automated trains running between\n\n- Kelenföld Pályaudvar in Buda and\n- Keleti Train Station in Pest with 10 stations along the way.\n\nThey run quite **often** (2-5 minutes) during rush hours.\n\nThe older three lines (M1 underground, M2-red line, M3-blue line) meet at Deák Ferenc tér in the city centre.\n\nRead more [about Budapest Metro lines!](https://www.budapestbylocals.com/budapest-metro/)\n\n## 🚊 Trams In Budapest -The Most Important Tram Lines:\n\nBudapest has more than 30 tram lines, you can recognize them by their bright-yellow colour.\n\n### Trams No. 4 and No. 6\n\n- Tram 4 operates between Újbuda Központ and Széll Kálmán tér) **,** while\n- Tram 6 connects Móricz Zsigmond körtér and Széll Kálmán tér)\n\nThe two are among the busiest tram lines in Europe. Tram 4 and 6 have an almost identical route they just differ in a couple of stops in the Újbuda side near their terminis there.\n\nBoth services run along **Grand Boulevard/Nagykörút** and have stop at the entrance to [Margaret Island](https://www.budapestbylocals.com/margaret-island/) (Margitsziget).\n\n![trams 4 6 budapest](https://budapestbylocals.b-cdn.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/trams_4_6_budapest.webp)_Tram 4 & 6_\n\n💡 **Local Tip**: Trams 4 & 6 un at around **5-6 minute frequency** from 07.00 till 20. 00. **Tram 6 operates all night:** you can expect a tram car every 10 minute between 21.00 and 24.00.\n\n### Tram No. 2, 2B & 23 – One Of The Most Scenic Tram Rides In Europe\n\nTram 2, 2B and 23 run along the Danube, between\n\n- Jászai Mari tér (at Margaret Bridge Pest side) and\n- Közvágóhíd in IX. district. Tram 2 runs at every 3 – 5 minutes from 06.00 till 19.00 on weekdays, then every 9-10 minutes till 23.45 – 24.00. It operates silghtly less frequently on Sundays and bank holidays.\n\nTravelling by tram is **slower** but more spectacular than by metro, especially if you take tram No. 2. or 2B\n\nThese two lines travels along one of the city’s most scenic routes, the **Danube Promenade**.\n\n![budapest public transport tram2](https://budapestbylocals.b-cdn.net/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/budapest_public_transport_tram2.webp)_Tram 2 On The Danube Promenade In Pest_\n\nA [sightseeing tour](https://www.budapestbylocals.com/budapest-sightseeing/) by bus doesn’t come up to a ride on **tram No. 2**. You get a very good view of the [Gellert Hill,](https://www.budapestbylocals.com/budapest-gellert-hill/) [Castle Hill](https://www.budapestbylocals.com/budapest-castle-district/), the [Parliament](https://www.budapestbylocals.com/budapest-parliament/), not to mention the Danube and the graceful bridges (Liberty, Erzsébet and Cain bridges) over it.\n\nYou have to buy your **ticket** in advance and validate it onboard at the start of your journey.\n\nYou either find red punch-machines or orange automated machines.\n\nTrams run between **04.30** am until around **22.45** on weekdays. You’d better check the timetables at the stops. You’ll also see the route of the tram line there.\n\n### Trams No **.** 47 and 49\n\nTwo major lines connecting Pest with Buda:\n\n- **Tram 47** runs between Deák tér-Budafok Városháza tér,\n- **Tram 49** travels between Deák tér and Kelenföldi Train Station.\n\n## 🚌 Bus Services\n\nBudapest has a very **extensive bus route** system. I personally don’t like to travel by bus, but some parts of the city (e.g. Buda Hills) can only be reached by bus.\n\nDuring rush hours buses are **crowded** and they often get stuck in traffic jams.\n\n### Night Buses\n\nThe night services are marked with a three digit number **between 900-999**, e.g. 906. You can get on a night bus at stops marked with the black-and-white owl symbol\n\n![A blue public transport bus on the Chain Bridge](https://budapestbylocals.b-cdn.net/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/budapest_public_transport_buses.webp)\n\n💡 **Local Tip**: Tram 6 (between Móricz Zsigmond körtér and Széll Kálmán tér) also operates all night at around 10-minute frequency.\n\nYou can buy tickets from the driver but you have to pay a bit more (costs 700 HUF instead of 500 HUF of the single ticket’s price).\n\nYou have to press a button above the doors to **signal** that you want to get off at the next stop.\n\nYou’ll find the **stops posted** inside the buses, but if no one gets off or on, the vehicle won’t stop, so you may lose track of stops.\n\nYour best bet is to ask locals travelling on the bus; they’ll be happy to tell you where to get off.\n\nUnfortunately you don’t have to queue at the stops, so be prepared that particularly **locals** tend to thrust, in order to get on the vehicle. (Actually it’s true for all kinds of transportation in Hungary.)\n\nSee [timetable for night services.](https://bkk.hu/en/timetables/)\n\n## 🚎 Trolley Lines\n\nThere are **14 trolley bus lines** in Budapest. Trolleys are red coloured.\n\n![budapest by trolley bus](https://budapestbylocals.b-cdn.net/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/budapest_by_trolley_bus.webp)\n\nIt’s interesting that their **numbers start from 70**, according to the story the first line started operating on Stalin’s 70th birthday.\n\nTrolley buses operate until somewhere between 11-12 pm.\n\nYou can check the **timetables** at the stops, they’ll provide reliable information. Ticket validation is the same as on buses.\n\n## 🚃 Suburban Railway (HÉV)\n\nYou can travel by **HÉV** (green trains) to the outskirts of Budapest.\n\n![budapest public transport suburban railway](https://budapestbylocals.b-cdn.net/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/budapest_public_transport_suburban_railway.webp)\n\nThe Szentendre line might be interesting for tourists. It runs between Batthyány tér (it’s also on the red metro line) and Szentendre.\n\n**Szentendre** is a small, charming town right on the Danube bank. Don’t miss visiting it if you come to Budapest for a couple of days!\n\nTickets within the boundary of the city cost the same as discussed above. Outside Budapest you pay according to the distance you’ll cover during your trip.\n\nWithin Budapest (Batthyány tér – Békásmegyer), your normal single ticket or travel pass is valid. Beyond the city boundary, from Békásmegyer to Szentendre, you need a supplementary HÉV ticket, which costs 560 HUF. HÉV trains run every 10 to 30 minutes.\n\n## Public Boat Service (Discontinued)\n\nBudapest used to have a scheduled public boat service on the Danube (lines D11-D14, between Boráros tér and Római fürdő), running seasonally from spring to autumn. As noted above, this service **ceased entirely in 2023** due to high maintenance costs and has not been reinstated. If you want to see the city from the water, a sightseeing or dinner cruise is the way to go – see our [guide to Budapest Danube cruises](https://www.budapestbylocals.com/danube-cruise-in-budapest/).\n\n## Try The Special Vehicles!\n\nBudapest offers several **unique** means of transportation some of them dating back to the 19th century.\n\nTry riding at least on one of these unique means of transportation during your stay especially if you’re with kids!\n\n### Funicular (Budavári Sikló)\n\nTakes you up to Buda Castle from Clark Adam Square at the Buda end of Chain Bridge.\n\n#### Location\n\n- Lower Station: Clark Adam tér- , Budapest 1013 Buda end of the Chain Bridge, next to the tunnel\n- Upper Station: Szent György tér, between Buda Castle and Sándor Palace\n\n![budapest transportation funicular](https://budapestbylocals.b-cdn.net/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/budapest_transportation_funicular.webp)_Funicular-Buda Castle_\n\n#### Getting to the Lower Station of the Funicular:\n\n- use bus 16, 105, trams 19, 41, Upper Sttaion: bus 16, 16A, 116 will take you there.\n\nThe funicular – that is a UNESCO Wold Heritage Site along with the whole Castle area – has been operating since 1870.\n\nIt connects the riverbank with [Buda Castle.](https://www.budapestbylocals.com/budapest-castle-district/)\n\nYou can enjoy the amazing view during the 95 m long ride, the grade of ascension is 50 m.\n\n#### Operating Hours\n\n- The funicular rides all year long, every day between 08.00 – 22.00 (with the exception of maintenance on every odd week’s Monday until the works last.\n- Frequency: every 5 – 10 minutes\n- Last ticket sold: 21.50\n\n![the glass-walled ticket office of the funicular with the two Hungarian national flags](https://budapestbylocals.b-cdn.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/funicular_buda-castle.webp)_Ticket Office of the Funicular_\n\n#### Tickets For The Funicular:\n\n- Return ticket (adult): 5 500 HUF, discounted (age 3-14): 3 000 HUF\n- One-way ticket (adult): 4 500 HUF, discounted (age 3-14): 2 000 HUF\n- Combined Funicular + Boat return ticket (adult): 7 000 HUF, discounted: 3 000 HUF; one-way: 6 000 HUF, discounted: 2 500 HUF\n- Free for children under the age of 3 (Only max. two children under 3 per adult are allowed)\n- Last ticket sold at 21.50\n- **Note:** You can pay with **Hungarian Forints** in cash or with **bankcard** only at the Funicular’s ticket office.\n\n![people travelling on the Funicular in Budapest, the photo shows 3 cars riding down and 3 cars going up](https://budapestbylocals.b-cdn.net/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/funicular_budapest23.webp)\n\n**TIP:** You can buy [tickets online for the funicular here](https://siklojegy.hu/en/).\n\nPlease **validate** your ticket before boarding and also make sure you keep your receipt of the ticket purchase until the end of the journey and you till you leave the station.\n\n### Chairlift (Libegő)\n\nAddress (Lower Station): Zugligeti út 97., Budapest 1121, Distr. XII.\n\n![photo of the chairlift traveling up to Janos Hill in Budapest in spring, people are seating in 4 of the chairs hanging from the steel cable](https://budapestbylocals.b-cdn.net/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/chairlift_budapest2022.webp)_Chairlift (Buda Hills)_\n\n- **Getting to Zugliget:** Take bus 291 from Nyugati Train Station, get off at the termini\n- **Getting To The Upper Station (János Hill):** Take bus 21 or 21A from Széll Kálmán tér (trams 4, 6, M2 metro) then walk on the footpath (20-30 minutes)\n\nTravelling on the chairlift lets you admire the wonderful panorama of the Buda Hills.\n\nIt will take you from **Zugliget** up to **János Hill** – the highest peak of Budapest – or back down.\n\nThe **12-minute journey** is slightly longer than 1 km (1040 m) while the elevation difference is 261 m. The 2 600 m long cable has 102 double seat chairs hanging from it.\n\nNot recommended if you’re scared of heights!\n\n💡 **Local Tip**: Climb up the Erzsébet Lookout Tower to get an even more panoramic view.\n\n#### Operating Hours (Every Day, Exc. Maintenance On Every Even Week’s Monday)\n\n- January: 10.00 – 15.30\n- February: 10.00 – 16.00\n- March: 10.00 – 17.00\n- April: 10.00 – 18.00\n- May: 10.00 – 19.00\n- June: 10.00 – 19.00\n\n- July: 10.00 – 19.00\n- August: 10.00 – 19.00\n- September: 10.00 – 18.00\n- October 01 – 30: 10.00 – 17.00 (Oct 31: 10.00 – 17.00\n- November: 10.00 – 15.30\n- December: 10.00 – 15.30\n\n#### Tickets For The Chairlift\n\n- Adult one-way: 3 000 HUF, round-trip: 4 000 HUF\n- Student (age 15-25, with valid student ID) one-way: 1 500 HUF, round-trip: 2 500 HUF\n- Children (ages 3-14) one-way: 1 000 HUF, round-trip: 1 500 HUF\n\n### Children’s Railway (Gyermekvasút) – Between Hűvösvölgy – Széchenyi Hegy\n\nChildren between 10 – 14 years of age check tickets and give signals to the train on this special train line, hence the name: Children’s railway.\n\n#### Schedule – Operating Hours\n\n- The Children’s Railway operates all year round. From May till September: every day, September – May: Tuesday – Sunday\n- Departure times: Hüvősvölgy station: 1st train departs at 08.45, last train: 17.22, Széchenyi Hill station: first train departs at 09.45, last one at. 18.45\n- Frequency: every 40-45 minutes\n\nGreat for **excursions** in the Buda Hills especially if you are visiting Budapest with kids.\n\nThe train journey take **40 – 50 minutes** between the 2 terminis, but you can get off at any station t go for hiking and exploring the hills.\n\n#### Tickets For The Children’s Railway\n\n- Adult single trip ticket (no stopover): 1 000 HUF, transfer ticket (rebound trip with no stopover or one-way trip with one stopover: 1 800 HUF\n- Children ages 6 – 18: single trip ticket: 500 HUF, transfer ticket: 900 HUF\n- Family day ticket (unlimited travel for the day; max. 2 adults + 3 children, or 1 adult + 4 children): 5 000 HUF\n- Nostalgia surcharge ticket (for the steam-train service, in addition to your regular ticket): adult 400 HUF, child 200 HUF\n- Bicycle ticket: 500 HUF\n- Dog ticket: 500 HUF\n- Day tickets are also available in the MÁV+ app: adult 2 500 HUF, child (age 6-18) 1 250 HUF\n- Families with kids (2 adults max. 3 children): 5 000 HUF – unlimited number of trips\n- Free for children under age of 6\n\n📋 **Note:** You can buy your ticket at the station’s ticket office or on board the train. Only cash payment is available and only Hungarian Forints are accepted.\n\n### Cogwheel Railway (Fogaskerekű)\n\nThe Cogwheel Railway (also known as Tram 60) isn’t a special-fare attraction – regular BKK tickets and passes are valid on it, same as on any tram. A single ticket bought in advance costs 500 HUF (700 HUF if bought on board), a pack of 10 costs 4 500 HUF, and any daily/monthly pass also works.\n\n## 🚲 Transporting A Bike\n\n### MOL Bubi – Budapest’s Public Bike-Share\n\nDon’t want to carry your own bike? Budapest has a public bike-share system called **MOL Bubi**, with docking stations all over the city centre. The service recently upgraded to **Bubi 3.0**, bringing a refreshed fleet of bikes and an updated docking network.\n\nYou rent and pay for a Bubi bike directly through the **BudapestGO app** (the same app used for public transport tickets) – unlock a bike at any station, ride where you need to go, and dock it at any other station when you’re done. It’s a convenient way to combine short bike rides with the metro, tram or bus for longer trips across the city.\n\nIf you’d rather rent a bike for a full day or longer (with no docking-station restrictions), private rental companies around the city offer bikes from around 500 HUF per hour, or a flat daily rate – a good option if you want to explore further afield, like along the Danube embankments.\n\n### Bringing Your Own Bike on Public Transport\n\nIf you’re **adventurous** enough you can also go [biking in Budapest](https://www.budapestbylocals.com/biking-in-budapest/). You can carry your bike with you on the on several public transport services:\n\n- Suburban trains – in the back of a carriage (HÉV)\n- Tram 60 (cogwheel railway),\n- Buses 65, 65A and 165,\n- trams 59 and 59A\n- public boat\n\nYou need to buy and **validate a single ticket** (500 HUF) for the bicycle if you don’t have a [bike pass](https://bkk.hu/en/tickets-and-passes/prices/monthly-passes/bicycle-pass.88/) which is 540 HUF (you can buy it as a supplement for most seasonal passes).\n\n## Travelling Information For People With Physical Disability\n\nThere are **low floor buses** and trolleybuses on several routes in Budapest, low floor **trams** on the Nagykörút and the Public Transport Company (BKK) offers a special **door-to-door bus service**, which they operate in a taxi-like system.\n\nThey launched this service on 12th April 2010 with 5 minibuses, type Renault Master 2,5 dCl, which were specially designed to help passengers **with reduced mobility** to reach one part of the city from the other part.\n\nTo make transport for physically challenged passengers as simple and easy as possible, one of the minibuses is equipped with a **ramp,** and four with **hydraulic lifts** and there are also special hand-holds in the passenger compartment.\n\nAll five vehicles are **air-conditioned**. The seats are moveable on a so-called rail system, so the passenger compartment can be re-arranged to meet every requirement. There is convenient room for 14 people or for 4 wheelchairs, and 4 or 5 attendants besides them.\n\nPeople who want to use this service has to **call** the National Federation of Disabled Persons’ Associations (MEOSZ), **phone numbers:** +36 1 388-55-29, +36 1 388-23-87 or +36 1 388-23-88.\n\n## Planning More of Your Budapest Trip?\n\n[🚢\\\\\n**Budapest Danube Cruises** \\\\\nSee the city from the water – sightseeing, dinner, prosecco and party boats compared.](https://www.budapestbylocals.com/danube-cruise-in-budapest/) [🛁\\\\\n**Budapest Thermal Baths** \\\\\nMany of the city’s baths (like the Cogwheel Railway and Funicular routes) are just a ride away.](https://www.budapestbylocals.com/budapest-spas/) [🎫\\\\\n**Is the Budapest Card Worth It?** \\\\\nFree public transport plus discounts on attractions – our full breakdown of whether it pays off.](https://www.budapestbylocals.com/budapest-card/)\n\n![Avatar photo](https://budapestbylocals.b-cdn.net/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/cropped-LizzyBP-320x320.webp)\n\nAbout the author\n\n### LizzyBP\n\nLizzy is a Budapest native and one of the local voices behind Budapest By Locals. She shares first-hand tips on family-friendly sights, neighbourhoods, cafés, day trips and everyday Budapest life. She lives in the suburbs with her husband, two sons and two dogs, and spends much of her free time exploring the city, biking in the Buda Hills and baking.",

        "title": "Best Way to Get Around Budapest: Everything You Need To Know",
        "description": "# Best way to get around Budapest: What you need to know\n## Getting around Budapest: tips and tricks\n- **Take the Budapest Airport Bus to get from the Budapest Airport to the city center:** The most popular way to get from the airport into the city is by taking the Budapest Airport Bus, also known as the Airport Express or the 100E.\n- **Get a Budapest Card for unlimited travel**: Budapest Közlekedési Központ (BKK) runs all of Budapest’s public transportation, including metro, trams, buses, and even boats in the summer. BKK offers 24-hour travel cards for individuals, 24-hour travel cards for groups (up to five passengers), or 72-hour travel cards for individuals.\n- **Get around at night by train or night buses**: Budapest offers public transportation at night. The metro runs until midnight, and night buses run along specific routes once the metro, trams, and regular buses shut down, ensuring you can get home by public transportation from dusk to dawn.\n- **Avoid rush hour**: Public transportation can get crowded during peak hours, typically between 8:00 AM–9:00 AM, and between 5:30 PM–7:00 PM. It is best to avoid the busy streets during these times or expect longer transportation times.\n\n## Useful apps\n- **BudapestGO App**: The one-stop shop for BKK tickets and pass purchases. You can also plan your journey and check arrival times or traffic information here.\n\n## 1. Getting around by train in Budapest\n#### How to buy and use train tickets in Budapest\nThe BudapestGO app simplifies ticket and pass purchases: you select the ticket or pass you want to purchase, pay on the app, and then validate your ticket or scan your pass with the NFC sticker on the vehicle doors of BKK lines and at station entrances on metro lines without opening the BudapestGO app.\n\n## 2. Taking the bus in Budapest\n![Public bus stopped amongst cars in Budapest traffic](https://cdn.getyourguide.com/image/format=auto%2Cfit=cover%2Cgravity=auto%2Cquality=60/dam/nguyen-minh-aaxf227VD1k-unsplash-LOWRES.jpg)\n\nHop on Budapest's extensive bus network to get across the city and adjacent neighborhoods\n\nBudapest has an extensive bus network of over 200 lines, providing locals and visitors with frequent and reliable service from the suburbs to the city center. Various routes, including express services, do not serve all possible stops, so plan your trip and ensure you board the bus that gets you to your destination.\n\n#### How to buy and use bus tickets in Budapest\nBuses, trains, and trams share the same payment system. To purchase a ticket or pass, download the BudapestGo app and scan your ticket upon entering a vehicle.\n\n## 5. Using taxis and ride-sharing services in Budapest\n![Taxi parked in front of the taxi stand](https://cdn.getyourguide.com/image/format=auto%2Cfit=cover%2Cgravity=auto%2Cquality=60/dam/tomas-anton-escobar-hVtRHmPVocQ-unsplash-LOWRES.jpg)\n\nHail a taxi or order them on your phone for a fast commute across town\n\nYou can find official taxis in the streets of Budapest, but it is best to be safe and order a taxi over the phone. Ensure you get a ride from a reputable firm such as 6x6 or a city taxi. Otherwise, you can order a vehicle using Bolt or Uber to connect you to a driver within minutes. Be sure to compare prices and select the option that works best for you.\n\n## 6. Hourly car rental services in Budapest\n![Electric car available for carsharing in Budapest](https://cdn.getyourguide.com/image/format=auto%2Cfit=cover%2Cgravity=auto%2Cquality=60/dam/2048px-GreenGo_%28Budapest%29_in_2023.03-LOWRES.jpg)\n\nphoto: CAPTAIN RAJU\n\nUnlock a car and ride around in Budapest or take a day trip to a neighboring city\n\nYou can also pay per minute with no obligation to pay a monthly subscription or monthly fees, perfect for travelers looking to zip through the city or go on a day trip outside of Budapest.\n\n## **FAQs**\n### Does public transportation run all night in Budapest?\nBudapest offers public transportation at night. The metro runs until midnight, and night buses run along specific routes once the metro, trams, and regular buses shut down. This late-night service ensures you can get home by public transportation from dusk to dawn, especially after a night out in town on [weekends](https://www.getyourguide.com/explorer/budapest-ttd29/weekend-in-budapest/).\n\n### Is it safe to use public transportation late at night?\nUsing public transportation in Budapest at night is generally safe. However, take standard safety precautions: be aware of your surroundings, know your route, keep valuables secure, and avoid isolated areas when possible.\n\n### Are there any transportation passes in Budapest?\nBudapest public transportation offers 24-hour travel cards for individuals, 24-hour travel cards for groups (up to five passengers), or 72-hour travel cards for individuals. Travelers may also purchase the Budapest Card, which grants unlimited access to public transit for 24 hours, 48 hours, 72 hours, 96 hours, or 120 hours, and discounted entries to museums, thermal baths, and cultural events.",

        "markdown": "- [Explore Budapest](https://www.getyourguide.com/budapest-l29/)\n- Places to see\n\n- Things to do\n\n- Trip inspiration\n\n\n# Best way to get around Budapest: What you need to know\n\nAn essential guide to getting around Budapest, from travel passes for public transportation to the best apps.\n\n![Oscar O’Connor](https://cdn.getyourguide.com/image/format=auto%2Cfit=crop%2Cgravity=auto%2Cquality=60%2Cwidth=100%2Cheight=100/dam/Oscar_O_Connor-hCesiG5D.jpg)\n\nOscar O’Connor\n\nJun 22, 2026•10 min read\n\nShare on\n\n![Best way to get around Budapest: What you need to know](https://cdn.getyourguide.com/image/format=avif%2Cfit=cover%2Cgravity=auto%2Cquality=60/dam/christian-lue-3kx_20rKFQM-unsplash-HEADER.jpg)\n\n[Budapest](https://www.getyourguide.com/budapest-l29/) is straightforward to get around once you know the options available as a traveler. A smooth and often picturesque ride with the city’s public transportation will enhance your visit to its iconic landmarks, like [St. Stephen’s Basilica](https://www.getyourguide.com/st-stephen-s-basilica-l3697/), [Fisherman’s Bastion](https://www.getyourguide.com/fisherman-s-bastion-l3694/), or the famous [Danube River](https://www.getyourguide.com/danube-river-hungary-l104472/).\n\nBudapest offers excellent commuting options, including a fast metro system, an extensive bus network, and a tram ride that makes seeing attractions part of the ride. Whether visiting Budapest for the first time or returning for another great adventure, this guide will keep you updated on the best ways of getting around in Budapest.\n\n## Getting around Budapest: tips and tricks\n\n- **Take the Budapest Airport Bus to get from the Budapest Airport to the city center:** The most popular way to get from the airport into the city is by taking the Budapest Airport Bus, also known as the Airport Express or the 100E.\n- **Get a Budapest Card for unlimited travel**: Budapest Közlekedési Központ (BKK) runs all of Budapest’s public transportation, including metro, trams, buses, and even boats in the summer. BKK offers 24-hour travel cards for individuals, 24-hour travel cards for groups (up to five passengers), or 72-hour travel cards for individuals.\n- **Purchase a Budapest Card for unlimited travel and other perks:** Travelers may elect to purchase a Budapest Card, which grants unlimited access to public transit for 24 hours, 48 hours, 72 hours, 96 hours, or 120 hours, as well as discounted entries to museums, thermal baths, and cultural events.\n- **Bike-share with the MOL Bubi app**: Budapest offers a bike-sharing service throughout the city. Simply register on the MOL Bubi App and select the ‘occasional user’ option so you can pay as you go.\n- **Get around at night by train or night buses**: Budapest offers public transportation at night. The metro runs until midnight, and night buses run along specific routes once the metro, trams, and regular buses shut down, ensuring you can get home by public transportation from dusk to dawn.\n- **Avoid rush hour**: Public transportation can get crowded during peak hours, typically between 8:00 AM–9:00 AM, and between 5:30 PM–7:00 PM. It is best to avoid the busy streets during these times or expect longer transportation times.\n- **Explore on foot**: Budapest is a very walkable city and thrilling to explore. Go across the Danube and see both sides of the city by the water, or bask in the beauty of the city’s gorgeous architecture and energetic atmosphere that can only be felt on foot.\n\n## Useful apps\n\n- **Google Maps**: Plan your routes and find real-time walking or biking directions. It provides public transportation schedules and updates for Budapest’s metro, buses, and trams.\n- **Citymapper**: An excellent app for mapping out Budapest’s best public transportation routes. It includes live departure times, disruption alerts, and cycling and walking route options.\n- **BudapestGO App**: The one-stop shop for BKK tickets and pass purchases. You can also plan your journey and check arrival times or traffic information here.\n- **MOL Bubi**: The official app for Budapest’s bike-sharing service allows you to find the nearest bike stations, check bike availability, start your journey, and manage your account.\n- **GreenGo:** Carsharing apps like GreenGo let you rent vehicles for short terms, including per-minute rates.\n- **Bolt and Uber**: Bolt has been present in Budapest for much longer, but Uber has entered the ridesharing space in the city since 2024. Check both apps to compare prices and get to your destination directly.\n\n## 1\\. Getting around by train in Budapest\n\n![Metro street entrance in Budapest](https://cdn.getyourguide.com/image/format=auto%2Cfit=cover%2Cgravity=auto%2Cquality=60/dam/nelson-wong-Sn04C8sCX1Y-unsplash-LOWRES.jpg)\n\nTake a ride on the Europe's oldest metro line in Budapest and get to your destination quickly and smoothly\n\nBudapest’s metro is the fastest way to get around the city. There are four metro lines and fifty metro stations. Metro Line 1, built in 1896, is the oldest underground railway in Continental Europe. Budapest’s tram network is also one of the most extensive in Europe, and it is a joy to ride. Be sure to ride Line 2, which runs along the Danube. It is one of the most picturesque rides in the city.\n\n#### How to buy and use train tickets in Budapest\n\nThe BudapestGO app simplifies ticket and pass purchases: you select the ticket or pass you want to purchase, pay on the app, and then validate your ticket or scan your pass with the NFC sticker on the vehicle doors of BKK lines and at station entrances on metro lines without opening the BudapestGO app.\n\n## 2\\. Taking the bus in Budapest\n\n![Public bus stopped amongst cars in Budapest traffic](https://cdn.getyourguide.com/image/format=auto%2Cfit=cover%2Cgravity=auto%2Cquality=60/dam/nguyen-minh-aaxf227VD1k-unsplash-LOWRES.jpg)\n\nHop on Budapest's extensive bus network to get across the city and adjacent neighborhoods\n\nBudapest has an extensive bus network of over 200 lines, providing locals and visitors with frequent and reliable service from the suburbs to the city center. Various routes, including express services, do not serve all possible stops, so plan your trip and ensure you board the bus that gets you to your destination.\n\n#### How to buy and use bus tickets in Budapest\n\nBuses, trains, and trams share the same payment system. To purchase a ticket or pass, download the BudapestGo app and scan your ticket upon entering a vehicle.\n\n## 3\\. Getting around Budapest by bike\n\n![Pedestrian standing in front of a city bike](https://cdn.getyourguide.com/image/format=auto%2Cfit=cover%2Cgravity=auto%2Cquality=60/dam/m-rennim-pOTkx8JjAw4-unsplash-LOWRES.jpg)\n\nGet access to Budapest's city bikes within a few swipes on the MOL Bubi app\n\nBudapest is a cycle-friendly city with over 200 kilometers of bike paths and lanes that make traveling on wheels safe and clear for riders. Travelers love taking the bike route that crosses the city along the Danube River, exploring various [Budapest neighborhoods](https://www.getyourguide.com/explorer/budapest-ttd29/best-neighborhoods-in-budapest/), pedaling past the beautiful buildings, and discovering the many hidden gems.\n\n### Renting Bikes in Budapest\n\nMOL Bubi is an app that allows users to rent city bikes parked in stations around the city. Download the app, register your number, pick up a bike, and start your journey. You will pay as you go at 40 HUF per minute.\n\n## 4\\. Getting about Budapest by boat\n\n![River cruise on the Danube with the cathedral in sight](https://cdn.getyourguide.com/image/format=auto%2Cfit=cover%2Cgravity=auto%2Cquality=60/dam/clary-garcia-zNs-aEIIkK8-unsplash-LOWRES.jpg)\n\nSkip the traffic and hop on a ferry, a scenic and relaxing way to travel\n\nIn the summer, BKK operates ferry boats that run along the Danube River with various stops along the river banks from Csepel-Királyerdő to Soroksár. Traveling by boat is not the fastest mode of transportation. Still, it is undoubtedly a memorable experience and a must-try when visiting due to the beautiful views of [Budapest landmarks](https://www.getyourguide.com/explorer/budapest-ttd29/landmarks-in-budapest/) such as Castle Garde Bazaar, a great [family-friendly activity](https://www.getyourguide.com/buda-hills-l111022/family-friendly-activities-tc1094/), the Hungarian Parliament, and [Margaret Island](https://www.getyourguide.com/margaret-island-l4982/) as you float down the Danube.\n\n#### How to buy and use ferry tickets in Budapest\n\nBKK also runs the ferry boat, so, like with the metro and buses, visitors can use the BudapestGO app to purchase tickets or travel cards. The Budapest Pass is also accepted during the validity period.\n\n## 5\\. Using taxis and ride-sharing services in Budapest\n\n![Taxi parked in front of the taxi stand](https://cdn.getyourguide.com/image/format=auto%2Cfit=cover%2Cgravity=auto%2Cquality=60/dam/tomas-anton-escobar-hVtRHmPVocQ-unsplash-LOWRES.jpg)\n\nHail a taxi or order them on your phone for a fast commute across town\n\nYou can find official taxis in the streets of Budapest, but it is best to be safe and order a taxi over the phone. Ensure you get a ride from a reputable firm such as 6x6 or a city taxi. Otherwise, you can order a vehicle using Bolt or Uber to connect you to a driver within minutes. Be sure to compare prices and select the option that works best for you.\n\n## 6\\. Hourly car rental services in Budapest\n\n![Electric car available for carsharing in Budapest](https://cdn.getyourguide.com/image/format=auto%2Cfit=cover%2Cgravity=auto%2Cquality=60/dam/2048px-GreenGo_%28Budapest%29_in_2023.03-LOWRES.jpg)\n\nphoto: CAPTAIN RAJU\n\nUnlock a car and ride around in Budapest or take a day trip to a neighboring city\n\nHourly or short-term car rental services can be found in Budapest. Look no further than GreenGo, the app that allows you to register and drive within minutes. You can also pay per minute with no obligation to pay a monthly subscription or monthly fees, perfect for travelers looking to zip through the city or go on a day trip outside of Budapest.\n\n## **FAQs**\n\n### What’s the best way to get from Budapest airport to the city center?\n\nThe most popular way to get from the airport into the city is by taking the Budapest Airport Bus, also known as the Airport Express or the 100E.\n\n### How accessible is public transportation in Budapest?\n\nBudapest has improved dramatically in recent years regarding accessibility for public transportation, but not all metros or trams are suitable for wheelchair users. Line 4 is wheelchair-accessible for the metro across the entire route, but the older metro lines only have a few stops with elevators and wheelchair access. Tram lines 4 and 6 are step-free and accessible for wheelchairs, but other tram lines have steps between the street and the tram. Most buses can accommodate travelers in wheelchairs as drivers can lower the bus and extend a ramp for access.\n\n### Does public transportation run all night in Budapest?\n\nBudapest offers public transportation at night. The metro runs until midnight, and night buses run along specific routes once the metro, trams, and regular buses shut down. This late-night service ensures you can get home by public transportation from dusk to dawn, especially after a night out in town on [weekends](https://www.getyourguide.com/explorer/budapest-ttd29/weekend-in-budapest/).\n\n### Is it safe to use public transportation late at night?\n\nUsing public transportation in Budapest at night is generally safe. However, take standard safety precautions: be aware of your surroundings, know your route, keep valuables secure, and avoid isolated areas when possible.\n\n### Are there any transportation passes in Budapest?\n\nBudapest public transportation offers 24-hour travel cards for individuals, 24-hour travel cards for groups (up to five passengers), or 72-hour travel cards for individuals. Travelers may also purchase the Budapest Card, which grants unlimited access to public transit for 24 hours, 48 hours, 72 hours, 96 hours, or 120 hours, and discounted entries to museums, thermal baths, and cultural events.\n\n### What’s the best mode of transportation for travelers in Budapest?\n\nExploring the city by foot is the best way to experience Budapest. You will get to know the city intimately and discover some hidden gems along the way while immersed in the beautiful architecture surrounding you.\n\n[![influencer-profile-image](https://cdn.getyourguide.com/image/format=auto%2Cfit=crop%2Cgravity=auto%2Cquality=60%2Cwidth=100%2Cheight=100/dam/Oscar_O_Connor-hCesiG5D.jpg)](https://www.getyourguide.com/explorer/creators/oscar-oconnor/)\n\nAbout the author\n\nOscar is an experienced travel writer with a passion for uncovering cultural hidden gems around the globe. From urban secrets to countryside wonders, he brings destinations to life with engaging storytelling and expert tips to inspire every traveler’s next adventure.\n\n### In this article:\n\n- Getting around Budapest: tips and tricks\n- Useful apps\n- 1\\. Getting around by train in Budapest\n- 2\\. Taking the bus in Budapest\n- 3\\. Getting around Budapest by bike\n- 4\\. Getting about Budapest by boat\n- 5\\. Using taxis and ride-sharing services in Budapest\n- 6\\. Hourly car rental services in Budapest\n- FAQs\n\nRead more about Budapest\n\n[![5 best neighborhoods in Budapest to really explore the city](https://cdn.getyourguide.com/image/format=auto%2Cfit=crop%2Cgravity=auto%2Cquality=60%2Cwidth=100%2Cheight=100%2Cdpr=2/dam/pexels-dash-dash-2147953268-29906515-HEADER.jpg)\\\\\n\\\\\nJun 23, 20265 best neighborhoods in Budapest to really explore the cityby Oscar O’Connor](https://www.getyourguide.com/explorer/budapest-ttd29/best-neighborhoods-in-budapest/) [![First time in Budapest: Everything you need to know](https://cdn.getyourguide.com/image/format=auto%2Cfit=crop%2Cgravity=auto%2Cquality=60%2Cwidth=100%2Cheight=100%2Cdpr=2/dam/pexels-trezellia-2600763-Header%20Desktop.jpg)\\\\\n\\\\\nJun 23, 2026First time in Budapest: Everything you need to knowby Emily Browne](https://www.getyourguide.com/explorer/budapest-ttd29/first-time-in-budapest/) [![Street food in Budapest: 10 dishes you have to try](https://cdn.getyourguide.com/image/format=auto%2Cfit=crop%2Cgravity=auto%2Cquality=60%2Cwidth=100%2Cheight=100%2Cdpr=2/dam/iStock-538749171-edit-HEADERDESKTOP.jpg)\\\\\n\\\\\nJun 23, 2026Street food in Budapest: 10 dishes you have to tryby Nicholas Martin](https://www.getyourguide.com/explorer/budapest-ttd29/street-food-in-budapest/) [![9 best free things to do in Budapest](https://cdn.getyourguide.com/image/format=auto%2Cfit=crop%2Cgravity=auto%2Cquality=60%2Cwidth=100%2Cheight=100%2Cdpr=2/dam/hungary-4544781-Header%20Desktop.jpg)\\\\\n\\\\\nJun 23, 20269 best free things to do in Budapestby Alec Hawley](https://www.getyourguide.com/explorer/budapest-ttd29/free-things-to-do-in-budapest/)\n\n## Read more about Budapest\n\n- [![First time in Budapest: Everything you need to know](https://cdn.getyourguide.com/image/format=auto%2Cfit=crop%2Cgravity=auto%2Cquality=60%2Cwidth=425%2Cheight=240/dam/pexels-trezellia-2600763-Header%20Desktop.jpg)\\\\\n\\\\\nHungary’s capital has everything you could want from a city: beautiful sightseeing walks, world-class cuisine, and an abundance of historic attractions that date back centuries. If it’s your first time in Budapest, many fun activities await you.Straddling the Danube River, Budapest is a city of two sides — Buda and Pest — each with distinct characteristics. If you’re after picturesque streets and historic neighborhoods, like Castle Hill, head to Buda. For some of the city’s best restaurants and its famous ruin bars (dive bars constructed in derelict buildings), it’s Pest. But to get a reel feel for Budapest, you must explore both areas — their best bits, along with important tips, dishes to try, and what to avoid are covered here in this first-timer’s guide.](https://www.getyourguide.com/explorer/budapest-ttd29/first-time-in-budapest/)\n\n- [![An all-season guide to the best time to visit Budapest](https://cdn.getyourguide.com/image/format=auto%2Cfit=crop%2Cgravity=auto%2Cquality=60%2Cwidth=425%2Cheight=240/dam/iStock-1488953464-Header%20Desktop.jpg)\\\\\n\\\\\nNicknamed the ‘Paris of the East’, Budapest is a glittering gem of Eastern Europe set along the Danube River. If you’re planning a trip to the Hungarian capital but can’t decide when to go, this month-by-month guide to Budapest will answer your questions on weather, seasonal highlights, and more. From warming up in the famous thermal baths during the winter snow, to getting lost in the Museum of Fine Arts, read on to discover the best time to visit Budapest.](https://www.getyourguide.com/explorer/budapest-ttd29/best-time-to-visit-budapest/)\n\n\n![](https://cdn.getyourguide.com/tf/assets/static/newsletter-signup/newsletter-background.jpg)\n\n### Discover the wonder of travel every week\n\nGet personalized travel inspiration, the latest travel hacks, and exclusive deals straight to your inbox.\n\nEmail\n\nSign up\n\nBy signing up, you agree to receive promotional emails on activities and insider tips.
