        "url": "https://justbudapest.com/budapest-public-transport/",
        "title": "Budapest Public Transport: Ultimate 2026 Guide & Map - Justbudapest",
        "description": "A single ticket covers one uninterrupted trip, but transfer tickets, 24-hour, 72-hour, or 15-day passes often provide better value for visitors.",
        "position": 6,
        "markdown": "[Skip to content](https://justbudapest.com/budapest-public-transport/#main)\n\n![A vintage yellow tram moving through the historic streets of Budapest](https://justbudapest.com/wp-content/uploads/vintage-yellow-tram-budapest-street-scene.jpg)Traveling back in time.\n\nDiscover the best ways of getting around the city – from metros, trams, and buses through taxi companies to eco-friendly transport alternatives. Budapest offers a wide range of great pulblic transport opportunities.\n\nKey Takeaways\n\n- • Budapest boasts a comprehensive and efficient public transport system (BKK), encompassing four metro lines, an extensive tram network, buses, trolleybuses, and even a funicular. It operates reliably from around 4:30 AM to midnight, supported by night buses routes.\n- • Tickets must be purchased and validated before your journey starts. A single ticket covers one uninterrupted trip, but transfer tickets, 24-hour, 72-hour, or 15-day passes often provide better value for visitors. The BudapestGO app is excellent for purchasing digital passes and planning routes.\n- • The city’s historic Tram 2 running along the Danube and the iconic Millennium Underground (Metro Line M1) are not just modes of transport, but sightseeing experiences themselves, offering incredibly scenic routes at the regular transport fare.\n\nCompared to other large European cities, Budapest is fairly easy to get around, mostly thanks to its extensive public transport system and some really useful eco-friendly ways that have become very popular lately. From metros and trolley buses to suburban railway lines and even boat services and electric scooters, you’ll surely find your favorite way of getting from point A to point B in a quick, efficient and affordable manner. So let us take a look at different ways you can make the best of your travel in this gem of a city.\n\n![A yellow tram passing in front of the majestic Hungarian Parliament Building](https://justbudapest.com/wp-content/uploads/scenic-tram-route-2-hungarian-parliament-building.jpg)One of the most beautiful tram rides in the world.\n\n## Public transportation\n\nGetting around Budapest by public transport is not only convenient but also affordable – if you choose the right **tickets or travel passes**. Most public transport services are operated by the **Budapest Transport Centre** (BKK – short for _Budapesti Közlekedési Központ, [www.bkk.hu](https://bkk.hu/en/)_), which manages buses, trams, trolleybuses, metro lines, and even some suburban railways (HÉV) within the city limits.\n\n![A yellow tram on lines 4 or 6 traveling along the Grand Boulevard in Budapest](https://justbudapest.com/wp-content/uploads/budapest-yellow-tram-4-6-grand-boulevard.jpg)The busiest tram lines in Europe.\n\n## Getting from Budapest Airport to the city center – your transfer options\n\nMost travelers arrive in the Hungarian capital via **Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport**, making it the first stop on their journey. Whether you prefer convenience, budget-friendliness, or speed, there are several **[Budapest airport transfer options](https://justbudapest.com/budapest-airport-transfer/)** to choose from — and selecting the right one can significantly improve the start of your trip.\n\nFor those opting for **public transportation from Budapest Airport**, two main bus lines serve the route: **bus 100E** and **bus 200E**. Bus 100E offers a **[direct shuttle service](https://justbudapest.com/budapest-airport-bus-shuttles/)** to **Deák Ferenc tér**, located in the very center of Budapest. It’s the fastest and most straightforward way to reach downtown — ideal for tourists with luggage or limited time. This **airport shuttle** requires a **special ticket** (currently (June 2025) priced at 2,200 HUF), which is different from the standard public transport tickets or passes.\n\nBus 200E, on the other hand, connects the airport to **Kőbánya-Kispest metro station**, the terminus of **metro line 3**, from where you can continue your journey into the city by metro.\n\nHowever, if you’re looking for a **more comfortable, door-to-door airport transfer service**, we also offer **[private airpo](https://justbudapest.com/quality-airport-lift/) [r](https://justbudapest.com/book-your-airport-transfer/) [t transfers](https://justbudapest.com/quality-airport-lift/)** that take you directly to your accommodation with no need to worry about schedules, luggage handling, or transfers. This is a great option for families, groups, or anyone arriving late at night or with heavy bags.\n\nBesides shuttles and private cars, there are also reliable **[airport taxis](https://justbudapest.com/budapest-airport-taxi/)** and **[long-term parking options](https://justbudapest.com/budapest-airport-parking/)** available, depending on your needs. Whether you’re arriving, departing, or organizing transport for a guest, Budapest provides a wide range of solutions for a smooth start and end to your visit.\n\n![The blue 100E Airport Express bus ready to transport passengers to Budapest Airport](https://justbudapest.com/wp-content/uploads/100e-airport-express-bus-budapest.jpg)Direct connection between the airport and the city.\n\n## Buses and night buses in Budapest\n\nWith **over 260 bus routes**, the **Budapest bus network** plays a vital role in public transportation across the city. Buses connect even the outer districts with the central areas, making them an excellent option if your accommodation is located further from the [main metro lines](https://justbudapest.com/budapest-metro/). Whether you’re heading to a tourist hotspot or simply trying to get to a **nearby metro station**, buses in Budapest provide a reliable and cost-effective way to travel.\n\nWhile buses can be slower during **peak traffic hours**, they are generally well-scheduled and punctual. For travelers who plan to explore **beyond central Budapest**, buses are often the best link to reach suburban neighborhoods or hidden gems off the usual tourist path.\n\nIf you’re out late exploring Budapest’s vibrant nightlife, you’ll be happy to know that **night buses** operate on most major routes, ensuring that you can always find your way back safely — even after midnight. These late-night lines are especially useful when **metro services stop running**, and they often connect with **key transport hubs** in the city.\n\nTo make the most of the bus system, you may want to consider using a **[Budapest Card](https://justbudapest.com/budapest-card/)**, which offers unlimited access to buses and other public transport. And don’t forget: having a **valid ticket or pass** is essential to avoid penalty, as **[ticket inspectors](https://justbudapest.com/ticket-inspectors-on-public-vehicles-in-budapest/)** frequently check passengers on both day and night buses.\n\n![A modern articulated blue BKK bus traveling on a Budapest street](https://justbudapest.com/wp-content/uploads/blue-mercedes-bkk-bus-budapest-city.jpg)Extensive bus network coverage.\n\n## Trams in Budapest – scenic, efficient, and iconic\n\nIf you’re looking for a scenic and stress-free way to get around the city, **Budapest’s tram network** is hard to beat. With one of the **largest and oldest tram systems in the world**, trams have long been a staple of public transportation in Hungary’s capital. Unlike buses, they typically run on dedicated tracks, meaning **trams rarely get delayed by traffic**, making them one of the fastest and most reliable ways to travel across the city.\n\nThe **Grand Boulevard (Nagykörút)** is served by tram lines **4 and 6**, which together form the beating heart of Budapest’s mass transit system. These lines operate with **modern, low-floor trams**, and are famous for their high frequency and round-the-clock service — in fact, **tram 6 runs all night**, making it a favorite among locals and night owls alike. The minimal difference in their routes makes this duo the most used tram service in Budapest — and even globally.\n\nFor a more nostalgic ride, hop on **tram lines 47 or 49**, which pass through **Deák Ferenc tér**, the main downtown hub. On weekends, **line 48** also joins in. These lines operate **retro-style carriages** that harmonize beautifully with the city’s historic architecture and **[iconic landmarks](https://justbudapest.com/capital-of-hungary/)**.\n\nOne of the true highlights of Budapest’s tram system is **tram line 2**, which was named one of the **most beautiful tram routes in the world** by National Geographic. Running parallel to the **Danube River** on the Pest side, this line offers **breathtaking views of Buda Castle, the Parliament, and Gellért Hill**, making it a must-ride for every visitor. It’s a perfect blend of **practical transportation** and **panoramic sightseeing**, especially if you’re not taking a **[hop-on hop-off tour](https://justbudapest.com/the-ultimate-hop-on-hop-off-sightseeing-tours-in-budapest/)** but still want to admire the city’s top attractions from your seat.\n\nAnd if you’re a fan of beautiful journeys, you’ll definitely want to explore **[more scenic transportation lines](https://justbudapest.com/scenic-transportation-lines-budapest/)** in Budapest — including funiculars, historic metros, and boat rides — all offering a unique way to experience the **vibrant charm of Hungary’s capital**.\n\n![Tram 49 on duty linking Kelenföld station with the heart of Budapest](https://justbudapest.com/wp-content/uploads/budapest-tram-49-kelenfold-route.jpg)An essential link to Buda railway stations.\n\n## Metros in Budapest – where history meets modernity underground\n\nBudapest’s [metro system](https://justbudapest.com/budapest-metro/) is not just a means of getting from A to B — it’s a journey through time. The city is home to **Metro Line 1**, the **second oldest metro line in the world**, which began operation in 1896 to commemorate the 1000th anniversary of the Hungarian state. Also known as the **Millennium Underground Railway**, this charming line runs beneath **Andrássy Avenue**, a UNESCO World Heritage site, and has preserved its original character through careful renovation. Step into one of its classic yellow carriages and enjoy the **vintage stations and art nouveau atmosphere** — it’s like time-traveling beneath the streets of Budapest.\n\nFor getting around the modern city efficiently, **Deák Ferenc tér** is your go-to hub. This centrally located square is the **main interchange** where metro lines **M1, M2, and M3** meet, making it a key transfer point in the heart of Budapest. Whether you’re heading to the Parliament, the Great Market Hall, or City Park, Deák is likely on your route.\n\nBudapest’s most recent metro addition, **Metro Line 4**(M4, a.k.a. green line), opened in 2014 and connects two major train stations: **Keleti Pályaudvar** in the east and **Kelenföld Vasútállomás** in the southwest. Designed with a **strikingly modern look**, this line showcases Budapest’s ability to blend historical legacy with cutting-edge infrastructure. If you’re arriving in the city by rail, Line 4 is often the fastest way to reach the center.\n\nFrom historic charm to sleek efficiency, **Budapest’s metro system** truly offers the best of both worlds — and is a must for anyone hoping to **experience the city like a local**.\n\n![The futuristic and award-winning architectural design of a Budapest Metro Line 4 station](https://justbudapest.com/wp-content/uploads/modern-architecture-budapest-metro-line-4-station.jpg)Budapest’s newest underground line.\n\n## Trolley buses in Budapest – quirky history and eco-friendly travel\n\nWhen it comes to public transportation in Budapest, **trolley buses** add a unique and nostalgic twist. Operating mostly in the **central districts of the city**, trolley buses are a quieter, more eco-conscious alternative to regular buses. With **15 lines in total**, they weave through key neighborhoods and offer an efficient way to explore downtown without the noise and emissions of fuel-powered vehicles.\n\nWhat often surprises first-time visitors is their **unusual numbering system**. The lowest number you’ll spot is **70**, and there’s a story behind that. The first trolley bus line was launched in 1949 and was numbered 70 as a symbolic gesture to mark **Joseph Stalin’s 70th birthday** — a reflection of Hungary’s political ties at the time. While the tribute is long forgotten by most, the numbering tradition has remained ever since.\n\nToday, trolley buses are a great option if you’re staying near popular spots like **Heroes’ Square**, **City Park**, or **the Embassy District**. Plus, they’re included in the standard [BKK ticket and pass system](https://bkk.hu/en/), so you don’t need anything extra to ride.\n\nWhether you’re a fan of **[sustainable travel](https://justbudapest.com/scooter-bike-renting/)**, curious about Budapest’s layered history, or simply want to avoid traffic, **trolley buses** offer a charming and practical ride through the city.\n\n![A red eco-friendly trolleybus stationed near the Keleti Railway terminal](https://justbudapest.com/wp-content/uploads/red-trolleybus-keleti-railway-station-budapest.jpg)A mix of bus and tram.\n\n## Boats – a scenic and relaxing way to discover Budapest\n\nYes, **you can explore Budapest by boat** too! BKK offers a **[sightseeing boat service](https://www.bkv.hu/en/content/bkv-boat-service-sightseeing-trip-in-the-heart-of-budapest-20240712)** in downtown Budapest, providing stunning views of the city’s landmarks and architecture from the Danube. Passengers can access information about the sights in 11 languages via QR codes onboard. The one-hour daytime round trip runs hourly from 11 a.m. to 7 p.m., stopping at key locations including Kossuth Lajos tér, Margaret Island, and Batthyány tér. Bicycles and pets (in carriers) are welcome, and the service is available all day with a single day ticket, even with breaks.\n\nThe evening sightseeing boat operates a non-stop round trip, departing from and returning to Kossuth tér without stopping at any other ports.\n\n![A BKK public transport ferry cruising the Danube river past the Parliament](https://justbudapest.com/wp-content/uploads/bkk-public-transport-boat-danube-parliament.jpg)Public transport on the water.\n\n## Suburban railways (HÉV) – connecting the city to its outskirts\n\nIf you’ve spotted a **green train with a white stripe** zipping through the city, you’ve seen the HÉV – **Budapest’s suburban railway system**. These lines are designed to connect **outlying towns and suburbs** to the capital, but they also include **multiple stops within Budapest**, making them a practical option for reaching less central neighborhoods, outside Budapest.\n\nHÉV lines operate similarly to metro lines and are managed by the **Budapest public transport authority**, BKK. Although not officially part of the metro network, they are integrated with the system, and **transfers are possible at key hubs** like Batthyány tér (line H5) or Közvágóhíd (line H7). If you’re planning to use Budapest’s **metro and suburban railways together**, make sure to check the appropriate ticket zones.\n\nEvery summer, the HÉV becomes the **preferred travel option to reach Sziget Festival**, as the H5 line takes partygoers directly to the island where the event is held. It’s a quick and affordable way to skip traffic and enjoy the journey.\n\n![A green HÉV suburban train waiting at a platform in Budapest](https://justbudapest.com/wp-content/uploads/green-hev-suburban-railway-train-budapest.jpg)Connecting the city to the suburbs.\n\n## Buda Castle hill funicular (Sikló) – A historic ride with a view\n\nFor a truly unique and scenic way to get around Budapest, don’t miss the **Castle Hill Funicular**, locally known as the _Sikló_. This charming piece of **historical public transport** has been operating since 1870 and remains one of the most iconic ways to reach the **[Buda Castle](https://justbudapest.com/buda-castle/)** from the **Széchenyi [Chain Bridge](https://justbudapest.com/szechenyi-chain-bridge/)** at river level.\n\nThe funicular glides up the steep hillside in just a couple of minutes, offering **breathtaking views** of the **Danube River, Pest skyline**, and the historic architecture that surrounds you. Whether you’re visiting the **[Castle District](https://justbudapest.com/iconic-sights-along-danube/)** for its museums, cobbled streets, or panoramic lookouts, taking the Sikló is not just transportation – it’s part of the experience.\n\nAlthough it’s not part of the BKK network (so regular tickets and passes are not valid), this **heritage railway** is well worth the small extra fee, especially if you’re looking for **memorable [**things to do**](https://justbudapest.com/100-unmissable-places-budapest/) in Buda**.\n\n![The historic Buda Castle Hill Funicular ascending the steep slope](https://justbudapest.com/wp-content/uploads/budapest-castle-hill-funicular-siklo.jpg)A fun and historic ascent.\n\n## Budapest has some unique public transport solutions as well\n\nBudapest has some really fun and festive public transport options during the holiday season. The **Christmas Light Tram** is covered in thousands of sparkling LED lights and looks magical as it rolls through the city. There’s also a **Santa Trolleybus** and a **Santa Bus**, both decorated for the holidays and often with little surprises for kids on board. These special rides usually run throughout December and are a hit with both locals and tourists. In the past, there was even a **LEGO tram**, which made the streets feel extra playful and fun.\n\nThe **Cogwheel Railway** is a unique train line that climbs up into the Buda hills, offering great views and a fun way to reach hiking spots like Normafa. It runs like a regular part of the city’s transport system, but feels more like a little mountain train.\n\nThe **Children’s Railway** is operated by children (under adult supervision) and takes you on a scenic ride through the forests of the Buda hills. It’s a charming and unusual experience that’s especially fun for families.\n\n![A tram decorated entirely to look like it is built from colorful LEGO bricks](https://justbudapest.com/wp-content/uploads/special-lego-tram-budapest-deak-square.jpg)\n\n## Tickets and passes for public transport in Budapest\n\n#### Where to buy tickets and passes?\n\nYou can purchase your public transport tickets or passes from:\n\n- The **purple BKK vending machines (for paper tickets)** found at metro station entrances and major hubs (payment by cash or card).\n- **Customer service points** at busy stations.\n- Some **bus drivers**, although this is more expensive and limited in ticket type.\n\nRemember: **tickets must be validated** before boarding (either by punching them in machines or scanning them digitally). Passes, on the other hand, don’t need validation — but you must always carry them, as occasional **ticket inspections** do happen, and fines for traveling without a valid ticket can be steep.\n\n![Looking inside one of Budapest's vintage yellow trams with wooden seating](https://justbudapest.com/wp-content/uploads/inside-vintage-yellow-tram-49-budapest.jpg)Riding in classic style.\n\n#### What kind of ticket should you get?\n\nour best choice depends on your itinerary and how long you’ll stay in Budapest. Here are the most popular options:\n\n- **Single ticket** – for one uninterrupted ride (no transfers allowed) (500 HUF)\n- **10 single tickets in pack** (4,500 HUF)\n- **24-hour travelcard** – ideal for intensive sightseeing in a single day (2,750 HUF)\n- **72-hour pass** – perfect for long weekends (5,750 HUF)\n- **7-day travelcard** – great for week-long stays or work visits\n- **monthly Budapest pass** – for longer stays\n- **[Budapest Card](https://justbudapest.com/budapest-card/)** – includes unlimited public transport and free/discounted entry to many attractions\n\nFor a complete list of up-to-date ticket types and prices, visit the official [BKK website](https://bkk.hu/en/).\n\nSome are eligible for **free public transpor** t in Budapest. Have to mention that, some special services, like the 100E airport shuttle require a separate ticket.\n\n- Children under the age of 14 can travel free of charge on BKK services, with proof of age required (e.g., student ID or passport).\n- EU, EEA (European Economic Area), and Swiss citizens over the age of 65 also qualify for free travel by showing a valid ID.\n- Blind or visually impaired passengers and one accompanying person may travel for free with official certification.\n- Budapest Card holders can also use BKK transport for free during the card’s validity period.\n\nFor understanding the price of tickets it is worth to check [this post about the Hungarian currency](https://justbudapest.com/hungarian-currency-forint/) and its exchange rate.\n\n#### What app should you download?\n\nMake your travels easier with [**BudapestGO**](https://go.bkk.hu/) application, the official Budapest public transport app (also available via website). It provides:\n\n- **Real-time departure information**\n- **Route planning**\n- **Vehicle tracking**\n- Route maps and disruptions\n\nWhether you’re hopping on a **tram, metro, or night bus**, this app is a must-have for stress-free city navigation.\n\n## Alternative transport options in Budapest\n\n## Taxis in Budapest – what you should know\n\nTaxis are a comfortable and widely available option for getting around Budapest, whether you’re heading to your [**hotel**](https://justbudapest.com/spa-hotels-budapest/), catching an early flight, or returning from a night out. All **official taxis in Budapest** must be:\n\n- Yellow\n- Clearly marked with the word **“** TAXI”\n- Equipped with a visible fare chart and a working taximeter\n\nThis uniform appearance makes it easier to **spot legitimate cabs** and avoid unlicensed or overpriced alternatives.\n\n#### Budapest taxi fares\n\nTaxi prices in Budapest are **regulated by the government**, which helps prevent overcharging. The fare (in June 2025) structure consists of:\n\n- **Base fare:** 1,100 HUF\n- **Distance-based fare:** 440 HUF/km\n- **Time-based fare (e.g. in traffic):** 110 HUF/min\n\nThere are **no night-time or weekend surcharges**, so pricing is consistent all week long.\n\n#### How to avoid taxi scams\n\nWhile most taxi drivers are professional and reliable, **scams can still happen**, especially around tourist hotspots. To stay safe:\n\n- **Avoid hailing taxis on the street** in front of train stations, bars, or major attractions\n- **Use official taxi apps** or phone dispatch services from trusted companies\n- **Pre-book your ride** through a reliable service provider (like us 😉)\n\nFor safe and stress-free travel, you can **[book your Budapest airport transfer](https://justbudapest.com/book-your-airport-transfer/) or city ride with us** – our prices are transparent, our vehicles clean and comfortable, and our drivers speak English.\n\n![A licensed yellow taxi waiting outside the impressive Keleti Railway Station](https://justbudapest.com/wp-content/uploads/licensed-yellow-taxi-cab-keleti-station-budapest.jpg)Always opt for official yellow cabs.\n\n#### Bolt – the most popular ride-hailing app in Budapest\n\nSince **Uber is no longer available in Hungary**, **[Bolt](https://bolt.eu/en-hu/cities/budapest/?gad_source=1&gad_campaignid=19782400484&gbraid=0AAAAADj1riYG7jwJF9oqJ2gyYlfye7AuP&gclid=CjwKCAjw_pDBBhBMEiwAmY02NiDepnNlRNXGrTlguFleVt1gTF0r8PTXUev262iIn_rezqCq_oiFoxoC5PEQAvD_BwE)** has become the go-to alternative for ride-hailing in Budapest. It’s widely used by both locals and tourists thanks to its **affordable fares** and **user-friendly app**.\n\nUsing Bolt is easy:\n\n- Just **download the app** from your app store\n- Register your **credit or debit card**\n- And you’re ready to **order a ride** to anywhere in the city — including **Budapest Airport**, tourist attractions, or your accommodation\n\nBolt rides are usually **cheaper than traditional taxis**, and you can see the estimated fare in advance, which helps avoid unexpected surprises. It’s also a great option during **peak hours** or **late-night outings** when public transport is limited.\n\n## MOL Bubi – explore Budapest by bike\n\nFeeling active? Budapest has become increasingly **bike-friendly** in recent years, making cycling one of the most enjoyable ways to discover the city. Whether you’re commuting or sightseeing, **[MOL Bubi](https://molbubi.hu/en/)** offers easy, app-based bike rentals throughout the city.\n\n**MOL Bubi** is the official bike-sharing system of Budapest, operated by BKK. With **over 2,000 bright green bikes** and **more than 200 docking stations**, it’s a convenient option if you’re staying near the city center or major transport hubs. Download the app, register, and you can rent a bike within minutes. Pricing is flexible: there’s a **daily, monthly, or pay-as-you-go** option, and rides under 30 minutes are often free with a pass.\n\nMOL Bubi is perfect for discovering places like **[Margaret Island](https://justbudapest.com/margaret-island-budapest/)**, the **Danube promenade**, or the **[Buda Castle](https://justbudapest.com/buda-castle/) area** at your own pace.\n\n## Lime e-scooters – Eco-friendly urban mobility in Budapest\n\nPrefer a more relaxed, yet still [eco-conscious way to get around](https://justbudapest.com/scooter-bike-renting/) Budapest? [**Lime electric scooters**](https://www.li.me/hu-hu) offer a fun and flexible solution. With their growing presence in the city, these **shared e-scooters** are perfect for short rides or covering the “last mile” between public transport stops and your destination.\n\nAll you need to do is **download the Lime app**, register, and unlock a nearby scooter with your phone. No bike lanes? No problem **.** Lime scooters are allowed on bike paths and smaller streets, making them a great option for quick inner-city travel.\n\nWhether you’re commuting, sightseeing, or just cruising through the downtown, Lime helps you avoid traffic and reduce your carbon footprint at the same time. Make sure to check the app for **real-time scooter availability** and local riding zones before you start your ride.\n\n![A row of green Lime electric scooters parked and ready for rent in central Budapest](https://justbudapest.com/wp-content/uploads/lime-electric-scooters-deak-square-budapest.jpg)A quick way for short distances.\n\n## Hop-on Hop-off sightseeing bus tours in Budapest\n\nWant to explore all the **top attractions in Budapest** without navigating public transport or relying on taxis? Then **[hop-on hop-off sightseeing bus tours](https://justbudapest.com/the-ultimate-hop-on-hop-off-sightseeing-tours-in-budapest/)** are your ideal choice. These comfortable, air-conditioned double-decker buses offer a convenient way to discover the city’s highlights at your own pace.\n\nFrom **Heroes’ Square** to the **Buda Castle**, and from the **Hungarian Parliament** to **Gellért Hill**, these tours cover all the must-see locations – and you’re free to hop off whenever something catches your eye. Buses run regularly, so you can continue your journey whenever you’re ready.\n\nThese sightseeing buses also pass by many of **Budapest’s famous statues**, each with its own story tied to the city’s rich history. If you’re curious about the people and events behind the monuments, or just want to soak in the city’s vibe from an open-top bus, this is a great option.\n\n**Pro tip:** Our [Budapest on a Rainy Day](https://justbudapest.com/budapest-rainy-day/) guide helps you find the best indoor activities even in bad weather.\n\n**Pro tip:** To ensure a respectful and smooth visit, read our [Budapest Culture & Etiquette](https://justbudapest.com/budapest-culture-etiquette/) guide before you start.\n\n**Pro tip:** Conveniently located near the Grand Boulevard, the [Radisson Blu Béke](https://justbudapest.com/radisson-blu-beke-hotel-budapest/) is a perfect base for exploring.\n\n**Pro tip:** The [Hilton Garden Inn](https://justbudapest.com/hilton-garden-inn-budapest-city-centre/) is perfectly located for access to the main metro lines.\n\n**Pro tip:** The historic [Hotel Nemzeti](https://justbudapest.com/hotel-nemzeti-budapest/) on the Grand Boulevard is great for the 24/7 tram lines.\n\n## FAQ\n\n#### What is the best way to use public transport in Budapest?\n\nA: The best way to use public transport in Budapest is through the BKK services (centre for budapest transport, [bkk.hu](https://bkk.hu/en/)), which include buses, trams, and the Budapest metro. You can purchase tickets from vending machines, tobacconists, or through the BudapestGO application for convenience.\n\n#### How does the Budapest Card work for public transport?\n\nA: The Budapest Card provides unlimited travel on all public transport services within Budapest, including the metro, buses, and trams. It also offers discounts at various attractions and is valid for a specified number of days.\n\n#### What are the different types and prices of tickets available for Budapest transport?\n\nA: Several types of tickets are available for Budapest transport, including single tickets, 10-ride tickets, and day passes. Prices vary based on the type of ticket and whether you are eligible for a discount, such as for students or seniors.\n\n#### How can I validate my ticket for public transport in Budapest?\n\nA: To validate your ticket for public transport in Budapest, you must stamp it at the validation machine before boarding. For electronic tickets purchased via the BudapestGO application, validation is automatic upon activation.\n\n#### What happens if I do not validate my ticket on Budapest public transport?\n\nA: If you do not validate your ticket, you may be subject to a penalty fare when checked by transport staff. It is essential to ensure your ticket is validated to avoid additional charges.\n\n#### Is there free public transport for certain groups in Budapest?\n\nA: Yes, certain groups, such as children under the age of 6, can travel for free on Budapest public transport. Additionally, there are discounts available for students and seniors, which can be applied to regular fare prices.\n\n#### How can I find my way around using public transport in Budapest?\n\nA: You can use a map available at stations or download the BudapestGO application for real-time updates and route planning. Google Maps also provides information on public transport routes and schedules in Budapest.\n\n#### Are there public transport services that connect the airport and the city centre?\n\nA: Yes, there are public transport services, including buses and taxis, that connect the airport to the city centre. The 100E bus is a direct service linking Budapest Airport with major points in the city.\n\n#### What types of vehicles are used in Budapest public transport?\n\nA: Budapest public transport includes various types of vehicles such as buses, trams, trolleybuses, and the metro. The M1 line of the metro, for example, opened in 1896 as part of the Hungarian Millennium celebrations and is one of the oldest metro lines in the world.\n\n## Recommended Posts\n\n- [![March in Budapest](https://justbudapest.com/wp-content/uploads/March-1-768x644.png)](https://justbudapest.com/budapest-in-march-a-time-for-unpredictable-fun/)\n\n\n\n\n\nVisit Budapest in March as the city awakens for spring!         "url": "https://emaginetours.com/blog/ultimate-public-transportation-guide-to-budapest/",
        "title": "The Ultimate Public Transportation Guide to Budapest | E-Magine",
        "description": "**GET 15% OFF  using the promo code SUNSHINE**\n\nCart\n\nFareHarbor\n\n0\n\nCheckout\n\n[![](https://emaginetours.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/emagine_logo_rides_horizontal.png)](https://emaginetours.com/)\n\n**- [+36 30 859 9587](tel:+36308599587)** **- [hello@emaginetravel.com](mailto:hello@emaginetravel.com)**\n\n**- [REVIEWS](https://emaginetours.com/our-reviews/)** **- [BLOG](https://emaginetours.com/blog/)**\n\n[tiktok](https://www.tiktok.com/@emagineridesbp)[facebook](https://www.facebook.com/emaginetours/)[instagram](https://instagram.com/emaginerides)\n\n[![en](https://emaginetours.com/wp-content/plugins/sitepress-multilingual-cms/res/flags/en.png)](https://emaginetours.com/blog/ultimate-public-transportation-guide-to-budapest/)\n\nIn Budapest, history meets modernity with remarkable results. The more time you spend planning your trip to Budapest, the longer your list of must-visit places will become!\n\nBut how will you get to them all? What is Budapest’s public transportation system like? That’s where this guide comes in! At E-Magine, we’re not only locals, but also leaders in [guided e-scooter tours in Budapest](https://emaginetours.com/guided-escooter-tours-budapest/) and [Budapest e-scooter rentals](https://emaginetours.com/monsteroller-escooter-rentals/). You can rest assured, we know all the best places and how to get to them!\n\nWe’ve used our local knowledge and insights to write this ultimate public transport guide to Budapest. Scroll down to find out more about how to get around our city — and if any questions come to mind as you read, please just [contact us](https://emaginetours.com/contact/) for the answers you need.\n\n![A group of five people riding electric scooters on a street, with one person in the foreground taking a selfie. The background features a stone building with large windows.](https://emaginetours.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/budapest-all-in-tour-05-1.jpeg)\n\n## Download the BudapestGO App!\nBefore we go any further, let us make one important recommendation — download the [BudapestGO app](https://bkk.hu/en/tickets-and-passes/budapestgo/)! This is the go-to app for journey planning, purchasing tickets, and real-time schedules. It’s available in an English language version too!\n\nWhen using the app, remember to scan your QR code BEFORE boarding your vehicle!\n\nWhile the BudapestGO app is great for buying local public transport tickets in Budapest, if you want to purchase intercity train or long‑distance bus tickets across Hungary, the official [MÁV+ app](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=hu.mav.emmapp&hl=hu) lets you do that easily on your phone — in English and without queueing at the station.\n\n[Trainline](https://www.thetrainline.com/en-us/trains/europe) offers a convenient platform for travellers arriving in Budapest by train or continuing their journey across Europe, partnering with over 270 rail and coach companies to provide easy access to thousands of destinations in 45 countries.\n\n## Getting Around Using the Budapest Metro\nThe Budapest Metro, inaugurated in 1896, holds the title of being the first underground railway system in continental Europe. With four lines serving the city, the metro is a fast and convenient way to zip between major landmarks.\n\nLine 1 (yellow), the oldest in the city and a [UNESCO World Heritage Site](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/400/), takes you along the iconic Andrássy Avenue, connecting Heroes’ Square with the city centre. Lines 2 (red) and 3 (blue) form the backbone of the metro system, crisscrossing the city and reaching key hubs like Deák Ferenc tér, where they intersect. Line 4 (green), the newest addition completed in 2014, provides swift access to the eastern and western parts of the city.\n\nYou can purchase metro tickets at machines in the stations, at the few existing ticket offices (such as Keleti railway station), or in the [BudapestGO app](https://bkk.hu/en/tickets-and-passes/budapestgo/). You must validate your ticket before entering the platform and your train, and keep it until your journey has ended.\n\nWhen it comes to ticket types, you can choose from:\n\n- Single Ticket\n- 30-Minute Ticket\n- 90-Minute Ticket\n- Travelcards (24 or 72-hour)\n\n## Travelling on Budapest Buses\nWith over 200 lines, Budapest’s bus network offers extensive coverage, reaching even the most remote corners of the city. Our city’s buses are blue, although you can also find red trolleybuses operating in Pest.\n\nIn reality, most tourists don’t need to board a bus to explore the historic centre and all the [cool and unusual things to do in Budapest](https://www.emaginetours.com/discover/what-are-cool-and-unusual-things-to-do-in-budapest/). However, the 100E bus offers a cost-effective and direct connection from Liszt Ferenc Airport straight to the city centre, with its final stop at Deák Ferenc tér. This makes it an easy way to start your visit before exploring the city. We cover the Airport Express below!\n\nIf you arrive on the 100E, you’ll be just steps away from us — our shop is located near Deák Ferenc Square at Bécsi Street 8. Here, you can conveniently store your luggage via the [Bounce app](https://bounce.com/ls/app), [rent an e-scooter](https://emaginetours.com/monsteroller-escooter-rentals/), or join one of our [guided tours](https://emaginetours.com/guided-escooter-tours-budapest/) by e-scooter — a fun and efficient way to discover Budapest right after you land.\n\nUnlike the metro, buses provide windows to admire the views, and they’re a great way to experience a slice of local life. Buses are punctual and frequent during the day; after around 11:30 pm, a night bus service (buses numbered in the 900s) begins.\n\n## Riding the Iconic Trams in Budapest\nThe famous yellow trams trundling through the streets of Budapest offer a picturesque way to explore the city. Budapest has one of Europe’s largest tram networks, with dozens of routes spanning the city and making it easy to explore both central and outer neighbourhoods.\n\nTrams 2, 4, and 6 are particularly popular among tourists. The number 2 offers a scenic route along the banks of the Danube on the Pest side of the river. It passes the Hungarian Parliament Building and the Chain Bridge while offering views of Buda Castle, Fisherman’s Bastion, and more across the river. Trams 4 and 6 run along the Grand Boulevard from Széll Kálmán tér to Újbuda Központ and Móricz Zsigmond Körtér, respectively. For the night owls, tram 6 operates all night.\n\nYou can validate your tram tickets using the onboard validation machines.\n\n![An orange tram travels across a green bridge at dusk, with cars following behind and buildings visible in the background.](https://emaginetours.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/budapest-tram.jpg)\n\n## Using Taxis in Budapest\nFor those seeking convenience and comfort, taxis are readily available throughout Budapest. Of course, they are more expensive than using the metro, buses, and trams. Opt for reputable, licensed companies or use ride-hailing apps like [Bolt](https://bolt.eu/en-gb/cities/budapest/) for transparency and ease of payment.\n\nWhile taxis are generally safe and reliable, be wary of unlicensed cabs and always confirm the fare before setting off. Ensure that your driver has started their meter before your journey begins.\n\n## The Budapest Airport Express Bus Service\nNavigating from Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport to the city centre is a breeze thanks to the Airport Express bus service. Hop on bus 100E for a direct and hassle-free journey to Deák Ferenc tér, in the heart of the downtown, where you can seamlessly transfer to the metro or explore nearby attractions on foot.\n\nThe journey takes around 40 minutes. During the day throughout the week, you can expect buses to arrive around every six to 10 minutes. In the mornings and evenings, this extends to every 10 to 15 minutes, and then 30 to 40 minutes at night.\n\nHowever, the Airport Express requires a separate ticket; you cannot use a regular single ticket for this journey. At the time of writing, a ticket for the airport shuttle costs 2500 HUF (€6-6.5). You can buy this ticket in the [BudapestGO app](https://bkk.hu/en/tickets-and-passes/budapestgo/), at ticket machines, or the bus stop for the Airport Express.\n\nAs we near the end of our guide to public transportation in Budapest, let us point you to some further reading. Our blog [Top Tips for Getting Around Both Sides of Budapest](https://www.emaginetours.com/discover/top-tips-for-getting-around-both-sides-of-budapest/) is filled with more local recommendations and insights that you will find useful in your trip planning.\n\n## See if the Budapest Card is a Good Fit for You\nAvailable in 24-, 48-, 72-, 96-, and 120-hour increments, this all-in-one pass is your key to unlocking the best of Budapest while saving time and money.\n\nYou can book your card online and then pick it up at a BKK Customer Service Centre in the airport (Terminals 2A or 2B) or the Budapest Info Point in Városháza Park between 9 am and 7 pm. For even more convenience, you can also purchase your Budapest Card in the [BudapestGO app](https://bkk.hu/en/tickets-and-passes/budapestgo/).\n\n![A group of people ride electric scooters on a cobblestone street next to a historic building, while others walk on the sidewalk under a clear, sunny sky.](https://emaginetours.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/buda-castle-tour-1.png)\n\n## Tips for Getting Around in Budapest\n- **Always Validate Your Ticket:** Before boarding public transportation, remember to validate your ticket to avoid fines. Validators are typically located near the entrances of metro stations or on board trams and buses. If using the app, scan your QR code BEFORE boarding!\n- **Avoid Travelling at Rush Hour:** To minimise crowds and ensure a more comfortable journey, try to avoid travelling during peak hours, especially on weekdays.\n- **Keep an Eye on Your Belongings:** While Budapest is a relatively safe city, exercise caution and keep your belongings secure, especially in crowded areas and on public transportation.",

SUNSHINE**\n\n\nCart\n\n\n\nFareHarbor\n\n0\n\nCheckout\n\n[![](https://emaginetours.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/emagine_logo_rides_horizontal.png)](https://emaginetours.com/)\n\n**- [+36 30 859 9587](tel:+36308599587)**\n**- [hello@emaginetravel.com](mailto:hello@emaginetravel.com)**\n\n**- [REVIEWS](https://emaginetours.com/our-reviews/)**\n**- [BLOG](https://emaginetours.com/blog/)**\n\n[tiktok](https://www.tiktok.com/@emagineridesbp \"tiktok\")[facebook](https://www.facebook.com/emaginetours/ \"facebook\")[instagram](https://instagram.com/emaginerides \"instagram\")\n\n[![en](https://emaginetours.com/wp-content/plugins/sitepress-multilingual-cms/res/flags/en.png)](https://emaginetours.com/blog/ultimate-public-transportation-guide-to-budapest/)\n\nIn Budapest, history meets modernity with remarkable results. As such, there are many things to see and do scattered across our home city, from the diverse wonders of City Park in the mostly flat Pest to the stunning views from Gellért Hill in hilly Buda. The more time you spend planning your trip to Budapest, the longer your list of must-visit places will become!\n\nBut how will you get to them all? What is Budapest’s public transportation system like? That’s where this guide comes in! At E-Magine, we’re not only locals, but also leaders in [guided e-scooter tours in Budapest](https://emaginetours.com/guided-escooter-tours-budapest/) and [Budapest e-scooter rentals](https://emaginetours.com/monsteroller-escooter-rentals/). You can rest assured, we know all the best places and how to get to them!\n\nWe’ve used our local knowledge and insights to write this ultimate public transport guide to Budapest. Scroll down to find out more about how to get around our city — and if any questions come to mind as you read, please just [contact us](https://emaginetours.com/contact/) for the answers you need.\n\n![A group of five people riding electric scooters on a street, with one person in the foreground taking a selfie. The background features a stone building with large windows.](https://emaginetours.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/budapest-all-in-tour-05-1.jpeg)\n\n## Introducing Our MonsteRoller E-Scooter Tours in Budapest\n\nOK, so our [Budapest e-scooter tours](https://www.emaginetours.com/guided-escooter-tours-budapest/) aren’t technically public transport, but they’re the best way to see our city’s highlights quickly while having fun. And best of all, a knowledgeable local guide will lead you through beautiful streets, picturesque parks, and along the banks of the Danube, providing a truly immersive experience.\n\nWe have crafted our range of tours to cover as many interests as possible. We even have a [Budapest Night Tour](https://www.emaginetours.com/night-tour-budapest-monsteroller/), so you can experience the magic of riding through the city when it’s quieter and lit by the gorgeous glow of streetlamps! And with our [Custom Private Tours in Budapest](https://emaginetours.com/budapest-group-tours/), we can tailor an unforgettable excursion exclusively for you.\n\nIf you prefer independent travel, look no further than our [Budapest e-scooter rentals](https://emaginetours.com/monsteroller-escooter-rentals/). You can rent one of our safe and sturdy MonsteRollers for one, two, or three hours, or even all day — and you don’t need a driver’s license to ride it either (the same applies for guided tours too).\n\nFind out for yourself what makes MonsteRoller e-scooters the fastest, most convenient, and most enjoyable way to explore Budapest. Check out [the best scooter tours in Budapest](https://www.emaginetours.com/discover/the-best-scooter-tours-in-budapest/) when have finished here to find out more!\n\n![A modern, empty subway station with a tiled, arched ceiling, columns, and benches. The walls are covered in a mosaic pattern, and a clock is mounted on the back wall.](https://emaginetours.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/budapest-metro-station.jpg)\n\n## Download the BudapestGO App!\n\nBefore we go any further, let us make one important recommendation — download the [BudapestGO app](https://bkk.hu/en/tickets-and-passes/budapestgo/)! This is the go-to app for journey planning, purchasing tickets, and real-time schedules. It’s available in an English language version too! The app will be your digital companion, making navigating Budapest’s public transportation network easier.\n\nWhen using the app, remember to scan your QR code BEFORE boarding your vehicle!\n\nWhile the BudapestGO app is great for buying local public transport tickets in Budapest, if you want to purchase intercity train or long‑distance bus tickets across Hungary, the official [MÁV+ app](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=hu.mav.emmapp&hl=hu) lets you do that easily on your phone — in English and without queueing at the station.\n\n[Trainline](https://www.thetrainline.com/en-us/trains/europe) offers a convenient platform for travellers arriving in Budapest by train or continuing their journey across Europe, partnering with over 270 rail and coach companies to provide easy access to thousands of destinations in 45 countries.\n\n## Getting Around Using the Budapest Metro\n\nThe Budapest Metro, inaugurated in 1896, holds the title of being the first underground railway system in continental Europe. With four lines serving the city, the metro is a fast and convenient way to zip between major landmarks.\n\nLine 1 (yellow), the oldest in the city and a [UNESCO World Heritage Site](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/400/), takes you along the iconic Andrássy Avenue, connecting Heroes’ Square with the city centre. Lines 2 (red) and 3 (blue) form the backbone of the metro system, crisscrossing the city and reaching key hubs like Deák Ferenc tér, where they intersect. Line 4 (green), the newest addition completed in 2014, provides swift access to the eastern and western parts of the city.\n\nYou can purchase metro tickets at machines in the stations, at the few existing ticket offices (such as Keleti railway station), or in the [BudapestGO app](https://bkk.hu/en/tickets-and-passes/budapestgo/). You must validate your ticket before entering the platform and your train, and keep it until your journey has ended.\n\nWhen it comes to ticket types, you can choose from:\n\n- Single Ticket\n- 30-Minute Ticket\n- 90-Minute Ticket\n- Travelcards (24 or 72-hour)\n\nYou can also buy a block of 10 tickets at ticket machines only. This is a convenient way to travel around the city and more economical than purchasing 10 single tickets individually.\n\nFind out more details about all metro ticketing options on the [BKK website](https://bkk.hu/en/tickets-and-passes/prices/).\n\nThe Budapest Metro provides a reliable, cost-effective service for getting around our city. However, the primary drawback for visitors is that you’re underground while travelling. This means that you miss out on seeing Budapest’s beauty and stumbling on hidden gems.\n\n![People on an escalator in a subway station, with a sign above indicating directions to \"Kőbánya-Kispest\" and \"Népliget-Központ,\" in Budapest. Posters line the walls on both sides.](https://emaginetours.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/people-on-the-budapest-metro.jpg)\n\n## Travelling on Budapest Buses\n\nWith over 200 lines, Budapest’s bus network offers extensive coverage, reaching even the most remote corners of the city. Our city’s buses are blue, although you can also find red trolleybuses operating in Pest.\n\nIn reality, most tourists don’t need to board a bus to explore the historic centre and all the [cool and unusual things to do in Budapest](https://www.emaginetours.com/discover/what-are-cool-and-unusual-things-to-do-in-budapest/). However, the 100E bus offers a cost-effective and direct connection from Liszt Ferenc Airport straight to the city centre, with its final stop at Deák Ferenc tér. This makes it an easy way to start your visit before exploring the city. We cover the Airport Express below!\n\nIf you arrive on the 100E, you’ll be just steps away from us — our shop is located near Deák Ferenc Square at Bécsi Street 8. Here, you can conveniently store your luggage via the [Bounce app](https://bounce.com/ls/app), [rent an e-scooter](https://emaginetours.com/monsteroller-escooter-rentals/), or join one of our [guided tours](https://emaginetours.com/guided-escooter-tours-budapest/) by e-scooter — a fun and efficient way to discover Budapest right after you land.\n\nUnlike the metro, buses provide windows to admire the views, and they’re a great way to experience a slice of local life. Buses are punctual and frequent during the day; after around 11:30 pm, a night bus service (buses numbered in the 900s) begins.\n\n## Riding the Iconic Trams in Budapest\n\nThe famous yellow trams trundling through the streets of Budapest offer a picturesque way to explore the city. Budapest has one of Europe’s largest tram networks, with dozens of routes spanning the city and making it easy to explore both central and outer neighbourhoods.\n\nTrams 2, 4, and 6 are particularly popular among tourists. The number 2 offers a scenic route along the banks of the Danube on the Pest side of the river. It passes the Hungarian Parliament Building and the Chain Bridge while offering views of Buda Castle, Fisherman’s Bastion, and more across the river. Trams 4 and 6 run along the Grand Boulevard from Széll Kálmán tér to Újbuda Központ and Móricz Zsigmond Körtér, respectively. For the night owls, tram 6 operates all night.\n\nYou can validate your tram tickets using the onboard validation machines.\n\n![An orange tram travels across a green bridge at dusk, with cars following behind and buildings visible in the background.](https://emaginetours.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/budapest-tram.jpg)\n\n## Using Taxis in Budapest\n\nFor those seeking convenience and comfort, taxis are readily available throughout Budapest. Of course, they are more expensive than using the metro, buses, and trams. Opt for reputable, licensed companies or use ride-hailing apps like [Bolt](https://bolt.eu/en-gb/cities/budapest/) for transparency and ease of payment.\n\nWhile taxis are generally safe and reliable, be wary of unlicensed cabs and always confirm the fare before setting off. Ensure that your driver has started their meter before your journey begins.\n\n## How to Use Budapest’s MOL Bubi Bicycles\n\nLike many other cities around the world, Budapest has a public bike-sharing program. Here, we have [MOL Bubi](https://molbubi.hu/en/). After registering online or on the app, you can find a docking station, unlock a bike and head out on a ride at your own pace. When you have finished, you must return your bike to a MOL Bubi docking station. If you leave your bike at an off-station location, you will have to pay an additional service fee.\n\nWhile there’s no doubt that MOL Bubi is a healthy, eco-friendly option, the additional steps required to ride make them less convenient than our [Budapest e-scooter rentals](https://emaginetours.com/monsteroller-escooter-rentals/) and [guided e-scooter tours in Budapest](https://www.emaginetours.com/guided-escooter-tours-budapest/).\n\nWith E-Magine’s rental option, you have true freedom to explore Budapest without the hassle and worry of having to find the nearest docking station. You also pay for your ride up front, so you don’t have to worry about the running costs while you make your way around our city.\n\nIf you’re looking for even more comfort and range, we also offer [e-bike rental](https://emaginetours.com/e-bike-rental-in-budapest/) in Budapest at our E-Magine stores, including our central location near Deák Ferenc Square. Our electric bike hire option is perfect for exploring larger distances along the Danube or reaching the Buda hills with ease — all without docking stations or time pressure.\n\n![A row of green bicycles with white identification numbers are lined up in an outdoor setting, ready for use.](https://emaginetours.com/wp-content/smush-webp/2024/04/mol-bubi-bikes-scaled-1-2048x1152.jpg.webp)\n\n## The Budapest Airport Express Bus Service\n\nNavigating from Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport to the city centre is a breeze thanks to the Airport Express bus service. Hop on bus 100E for a direct and hassle-free journey to Deák Ferenc tér, in the heart of the downtown, where you can seamlessly transfer to the metro or explore nearby attractions on foot.\n\nThe journey takes around 40 minutes. During the day throughout the week, you can expect buses to arrive around every six to 10 minutes. In the mornings and evenings, this extends to every 10 to 15 minutes, and then 30 to 40 minutes at night.\n\nHowever, the Airport Express requires a separate ticket; you cannot use a regular single ticket for this journey. At the time of writing, a ticket for the airport shuttle costs 2500 HUF (€6-6.5). You can buy this ticket in the [BudapestGO app](https://bkk.hu/en/tickets-and-passes/budapestgo/), at ticket machines, or the bus stop for the Airport Express.\n\nAs we near the end of our guide to public transportation in Budapest, let us point you to some further reading. Our blog [Top Tips for Getting Around Both Sides of Budapest](https://www.emaginetours.com/discover/top-tips-for-getting-around-both-sides-of-budapest/) is filled with more local recommendations and insights that you will find useful in your trip planning.\n\n## See if the Budapest Card is a Good Fit for You\n\nFor unlimited access to public transportation and discounts at some museums, restaurants, and attractions, look no further than the [Budapest Card](https://www.budapestinfo.hu/en/budapest-card). Available in 24-, 48-, 72-, 96-, and 120-hour increments, this all-in-one pass is your key to unlocking the best of Budapest while saving time and money.\n\nYou can book your card online and then pick it up at a BKK Customer Service Centre in the airport (Terminals 2A or 2B) or the Budapest Info Point in Városháza Park between 9 am and 7 pm. For even more convenience, you can also purchase your Budapest Card in the [BudapestGO app](https://bkk.hu/en/tickets-and-passes/budapestgo/).\n\n![A group of people ride electric scooters on a cobblestone street next to a historic building, while others walk on the sidewalk under a clear, sunny sky.](https://emaginetours.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/buda-castle-tour-1.png)\n\n## Tips for Getting Around in Budapest\n\n- **Always Validate Your Ticket:** Before boarding public transportation, remember to validate your ticket to avoid fines. Validators are typically located near the entrances of metro stations or on board trams and buses. If using the app, scan your QR code BEFORE boarding!\n- **Avoid Travelling at Rush Hour:** To minimise crowds and ensure a more comfortable journey, try to avoid travelling during peak hours, especially on weekdays.\n- **Keep an Eye on Your Belongings:** While Budapest is a relatively safe city, exercise caution and keep your belongings secure, especially in crowded areas and on public transportation.\n- **Don’t Forget to Download the BudapestGO App:** With this digital companion in the palm of your hand, navigating our city becomes so much easier!\n\n![Aerial view of Budapest showcasing the Danube River, the Parliament building on the river bank, and the city's historic buildings and rooftops with scattered greenery.](https://emaginetours.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/cityscape-of-budapest.jpg)\n\n## Book Your Spot on Our Budapest E-Scooter Tours!\n\nWe hope you’ve found this ultimate public transportation guide to Budapest helpful as you prepare for your adventure in Hungary’s capital. Spots on our [guided e-scooter tours in Budapest](https://www.emaginetours.com/guided-escooter-tours-budapest/) tend to sell out, so don’t miss out on the best way to explore our city and the #1 ranked outdoor activity in Budapest on Tripadvisor!\n\nIf you have any questions about our tours or [Budapest e-scooter rentals](https://emaginetours.com/monsteroller-escooter-rentals/), please don’t hesitate to [get in touch](https://emaginetours.com/contact/).\n\n[featured](https://emaginetours.com/blog/tag/featured/)\n\n[Prev](https://emaginetours.com/blog/best-things-to-do-in-budapest-at-night/)[Next](https://emaginetours.com/blog/things-to-do-in-budapest/)\n\nHey! How can I help you today?",
